# Atlas — full documentation for LLMs

> Atlas is a local code-intelligence CLI: one native binary that indexes a
> repository into a SQLite symbol and relationship graph and answers focused
> context queries (definition, callers, callees, imports, routes) in
> single-digit milliseconds and tens of tokens. Benchmark (Benchmark &amp; field comparison — refreshed at fc3b875 (2026-08-05)):
> 3.17× fewer answer tokens than the graph tool, pooled over 7 repositories,
> at caller-F1 0.865 vs 0.541. Version 0.1.54.
>
> This file inlines the complete consumer documentation. Canonical HTML pages
> live at https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/<slug>/ ; the interactive site is at https://atlas.aziro.com/.

- Product site: https://atlas.aziro.com/
- Benchmarks: https://atlas.aziro.com/#benchmarks
- GitHub: https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas
- Wiki: https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/wiki
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aziron/atlas
- GitHub Packages: https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/pkgs/npm/atlas


---

# What Atlas Does
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/tour/

# What Atlas does

Atlas builds a local index of a repository — its symbols, the calls and
references between them, the HTTP routes it serves and the history of each
indexing pass — and answers questions about it exactly, with a file and line
for every claim. The same index feeds a browser dashboard, a command line, an
HTTP API and AI assistants over MCP, so a person and an assistant read the
same facts. This page shows each area in one frame and links to its guide.
Every screenshot is from Atlas running on the public Go project
inference-gateway.

## Command Center

The dashboard opens on the **Command Center**: a summary of everything one
Atlas service holds. Tiles count recall savings, connected devices, skills,
events per minute and the service's own latency; a row below shows each
configured monitoring tool; a live feed on the right lists the newest events.
Every number is read from the running service, and every tile opens the view
that owns it. The navigation rail on the left reaches every other area.

![The Command Center with KPI tiles, the Observe row and the Live activity feed](assets/docs/tour/command-center.png "The Command Center.")

Read more: [The dashboard](dashboard).

## Code Map

The **Code Map** draws the stored graph five ways. **Clusters** packs the
whole repository as its folder tree; **Flow** reads one symbol with its
callers on the left and callees on the right; **Explorer** lists the same
relations with call-site evidence; **Workbench** (beta) is a canvas you
arrange and export; **Repos** draws which services call which. **Path
Finder** traces how one function reaches another, and **Resolve** maps a
pasted log line back to the code that emits it.

![The Code Map in the Clusters lens for inference-gateway](assets/docs/tour/code-map.png "The Code Map, Clusters lens.")

Read more: [Code Map and graph](code-map).

## Search and Ask

Press `/` anywhere in the dashboard to search every indexed symbol by name,
path or a word from its signature. **Ask Atlas** takes a question in plain
language and answers with the lines that answer it — the best passage first,
quoted and cited, then the other files that matched. For symbol questions it
adds an exact verdict, such as the number of callers. An optional AI answer,
written only from those passages, can sit on top.

![Ask Atlas answering how are allowed models enforced with a passage from config/config.go](assets/docs/tour/search-and-ask.png "Ask Atlas: the best passage for a question, quoted with its lines.")

Read more: [Search and Ask](search-and-ask).

## Ask Workbench

The **Ask Workbench** is a conversation about the codebase. Atlas gathers the
evidence — passages, definitions, routes, git history, and the tickets and
pull requests of connected sources — and a model you choose writes the
answer, citing each piece. The evidence panel lists every item the answer
rests on, and the server keeps each thread, so you can come back to it or
share its link.

![Ask Workbench answering which HTTP routes the gateway serves, with a routes table and citation chips](assets/docs/tour/workbench.png "A Workbench thread: the routes table, every row cited, and the evidence on the right.")

Read more: [Ask Workbench](workbench).

## Impact and Routes

Before you change a symbol, **Impact** shows what the change could reach over
stored call and import edges: every affected symbol, file and test, the
routes whose handlers fall inside that radius, and the call sites in other
indexed repositories. **Routes** lists the HTTP surface the index proved,
each route with its handler. The same answers come from `atlas impact` and
`atlas context` when you review a change.

![Impact for modelDenied: seven impacted handlers](assets/docs/tour/impact.png "The blast radius of modelDenied: seven symbols, each resolvable in the inspector.")

Read more: [Impact and review](impact).

## Change Lens

Every indexing pass is kept as a snapshot. The **Change Lens** shows the
timeline of snapshots for a repository and, for any pass, what it changed:
symbols added, modified and removed, files touched, call edges gained and
lost. With a single snapshot it says a diff needs two and gives the command
that makes the second. **Freshness** shows how current each index is.

![Change Lens for inference-gateway with one snapshot recorded](assets/docs/tour/change-lens.png "The Change Lens on a repository indexed once: one snapshot, and the command that records the next.")

Read more: [Change lens and history](history).

## Observe

Connect a log store, Prometheus, Jenkins or Tempo and an **OBSERVE** group
appears in the navigation: Log Streams, What Changed, Alerts & Metrics,
Builds, Incidents and Traces. Each answers a bounded question — the alerts
firing now, the log templates growing since a deploy, the build that failed —
and links what it finds back to the code that emits it. Atlas keeps templates
and summaries, not raw lines.

![Alerts and Metrics reading the public Prometheus demo: firing alerts and a bounded query](assets/docs/tour/observe.png "Alerts & Metrics against the public Prometheus demo.")

Read more: [Observe](observe).

## Connected Sources

Code is one source among several. `atlas source` indexes GitHub pull requests
and issues, Jira, Confluence, OneDrive, Jenkins, Prometheus, Grafana and Tempo
as virtual repositories beside your code, so a search or a Workbench question
can cite a ticket as readily as a function. The **Connectors** page configures
the monitoring tools: each card says what it unlocks, saving checks that the
tool is reachable, and credentials are stored as environment variable names,
never values.

![The Connectors page with Grafana Loki and Prometheus configured](assets/docs/tour/sources.png "Connectors: a Loki log pull and the Prometheus demo configured.")

Read more: [Connected sources](sources).

## Skills and Automations

A skill is a reviewed runbook an assistant can follow: steps, the parameters
it takes, its preconditions, how to verify it worked and how to roll it back.
**Skill Studio** turns repeated sessions into a draft; **Skills** moves each
one through candidate, validating and trusted, and only trusted skills are
offered to connected assistants. **Approvals** holds the requests that wait
for a person.

![The Skills view with one validating runbook: its steps, rendered SKILL.md and contract](assets/docs/tour/skills.png "A skill under validation: runbook steps, the rendered SKILL.md and its contract.")

Read more: [Skills and automations](skills).

## AI Assistants over MCP

`atlas bootstrap` registers Atlas as an MCP server for the assistants it
finds on the machine — Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini — and installs
an instruction to ask Atlas before searching files. The assistant then calls
the same tools the dashboard uses — search, symbol, impact, routes, logs and
more. When assistants reach Atlas through the service, the System page counts
every call, with errors, latency and the size of the answer.

![System per-tool breakdown: calls, errors, p50, p95 and estimated tokens for each tool](assets/docs/tour/assistants.png "System → Per-tool breakdown: every tool call the service answered.")

Read more: [AI assistant setup](assistants).

## The CLI

Every answer the dashboard shows is also a command of the single `atlas`
binary, with `--format plain` for people and JSON for scripts. Index, search,
ask for callers, trace a path, size a change, read the graph report, export
the graph, run the service:

```sh
atlas callers modelDenied --format plain
callers modelDenied  total 5
  ChatCompletionsHandler  method  api/routes.go:637  :: func (router *RouterImpl) ChatCompletionsHandler(c *gin.Context)
  ImagesHandler  method  api/routes.go:1194  :: func (router *RouterImpl) ImagesHandler(c *gin.Context)
  MessagesHandler  method  api/routes.go:842  :: func (router *RouterImpl) MessagesHandler(c *gin.Context)
  …
```

Read more: [CLI reference](cli).

## How the Pieces Fit

1. **Index.** `atlas index` parses a repository into symbols, edges and
   routes and stores them, with a lexical search index, in a local database.
   Each pass is a snapshot.
2. **Graph.** Every query — search, callers, path, impact, report — reads that
   stored graph. Nothing is guessed at query time.
3. **Surfaces.** The same graph is served four ways: the CLI, the dashboard
   and HTTP API of `atlas serve`, and MCP for assistants (`atlas mcp`, or
   `atlas serve --mcp`).

[Core concepts](concepts) explains snapshots, scope and output control;
[Getting started](getting-started) takes you from install to the first
answer.

---

# Getting Started
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/getting-started/

# Getting Started

This guide takes a repository from unindexed to queryable: build the local
index, verify it is healthy, run the core queries, and connect an AI
assistant. Atlas is local-first — everything below runs on your machine
against an embedded database, with no server or account required. For the
mental model behind these commands, see [Core Concepts](concepts).

## 1. Check Prerequisites

Confirm the binary is installed and on `PATH` before anything else, because
assistants and scripts resolve `atlas` from `PATH` too.

```sh
command -v atlas
atlas version
```

If either command fails, follow [Installation](installation) first. You also
need a local checkout of the repository you want to index; a git repository is
required for commit-pinned indexing (`--ref`) and the per-commit snapshot
history.

## 2. Index a Repository

Indexing builds everything Atlas knows about a repository: it parses symbols,
call edges, and routes, and persists the **knowledge graph** plus a lexical
search index.

```sh
cd /path/to/repository
atlas index .
```

Progress is printed to stderr while the run reports discovery and completion
stats. Results are stored in an embedded SQLite database in the repository:

```text
.atlas/atlas.db
```

By default the indexer skips paths git ignores (build output, caches,
vendored runtimes); pass `--gitignore=false` to index everything. The first
run parses the whole repository; later runs are incremental deltas. Use
`--reindex` to force a full rebuild, and `--ref` to index a specific commit or
branch instead of the working tree. See [Indexing and Reindexing](indexing)
for exclusions, watch mode, and the optional embedding pass
(`--enable-vectors`).

## 3. Confirm Readiness

Verify the index before relying on query results, so an empty or drifted
database does not silently return nothing.

```sh
atlas status
atlas stats
```

`atlas status` reports storage and version health: the schema and index-format
contracts and the per-repo snapshot format state. `atlas stats` reports graph
and index telemetry for the indexed repository. Look for your repository
identity, a current snapshot, and non-zero symbol and edge counts. Zero counts
or a missing repository mean the index did not build — see
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting).

The same index is visible in the dashboard. Run `atlas serve` and open
`http://127.0.0.1:3099/dashboard`. **Live Activity** records the indexing pass
with what it found — here inference-gateway, a public Go project:

![A Live Activity row: indexed inference-gateway, 307 files, 11092 symbols, 13900 edges, 71 routes](assets/docs/getting-started/index-event.png "The first index of inference-gateway, as Live Activity records it: 307 files, 11,092 symbols, 13,900 edges and 71 routes in about 54 seconds.")

**Workspace** (under CODEBASE) lists the repository with the same counts, its
index mode, when it was indexed and its status, with **Orient me** and **Map**
to start reading:

![The Workspace per-repository table with inference-gateway: 307 files, 11,092 symbols, 13,900 edges, 71 routes, full, indexed](assets/docs/getting-started/workspace-repo.png "The repository in Workspace, ready to explore.")

**Orient me** opens **Orientation**: the entry points the repository serves,
its most-connected symbols and its modules — the quickest way into code you
have not read before.

![Orientation for inference-gateway: graph counts, language bars, entry points and load-bearing symbols](assets/docs/getting-started/orientation.png "Orientation for inference-gateway: entry points on the left, load-bearing symbols on the right.")

[The dashboard](dashboard) walks through every view.

## 4. Run the First Queries

Each query answers a different question; pick the one that matches what you
already know.

Use `search` when you know words or phrases but not exact names — it is
code-aware lexical search (BM25 + trigram) over the symbol index:

```sh
atlas search "authentication middleware" --format plain
```

Use `symbol` when you know a name and want its definition(s) together with
its callers and callees:

```sh
atlas symbol NewServer
```

Use `callers` before changing a function's behavior or signature, to see
exactly which symbols call it directly:

```sh
atlas callers NewServer --limit 25
```

Use `refs` when a rename or type change is on the table — it lists call sites
plus type-use references (params, fields, returns):

```sh
atlas refs NewServer
```

Use `context` when reviewing a change — it builds a bounded review-context
bundle (16–32 KiB with the default `auto` intent) around the changed files:

```sh
atlas context \
  --paths path/to/changed-file.go \
  --query "review correctness and regression risk" \
  --format json
```

For the blast radius of a change — impacted symbols, files, and covering
tests — use `impact`:

```sh
atlas impact --paths path/to/changed-file.go
```

Run `atlas <command> --help` for the full flag list of your installed version,
or see the [CLI Reference](cli).

## 5. Connect an AI Assistant

Bootstrap registers Atlas as an MCP server and installs the atlas-first skill
and CLAUDE.md directive for every detected assistant (Claude desktop and CLI,
Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini), so assistants query the graph instead of
grepping. Preview what would be written first:

```sh
atlas bootstrap --dry-run
```

Then apply it:

```sh
atlas bootstrap
```

Bootstrap is idempotent — safe to run repeatedly. Use `--only` or `--skip`
(comma-separated agent lists) to limit which assistants are provisioned.
Restart the assistant after configuration changes, and run
`atlas doctor --verify atlas` to confirm the `atlas` on `PATH` — what
assistants launch — matches the binary you installed. See [MCP Tools](mcp)
for the tool surface assistants receive.

## 6. Keep the Index Fresh

Query results are only as current as the last index run. After meaningful
changes, run an incremental update:

```sh
atlas index .
```

For a foreground process that re-indexes on every file change (edits within
250 ms are coalesced into one update):

```sh
atlas watch
```

Reserve `atlas index . --reindex` for format changes or recovery, per
[Indexing and Reindexing](indexing).

## Where to Go Next

- [Core Concepts](concepts) — the graph, snapshots, workspaces, and output
  control that every command shares.
- [CLI Reference](cli) — every command and flag.
- [MCP Tools](mcp) — what assistants can call after bootstrap.
- [Configuration](configuration) — knob precedence and `atlas config`.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting) — empty results, drift, and recovery.

# Installation
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/installation/

# Installation

Atlas ships through five channels that all install the same native binary.
Pick the channel that matches how you manage software on the target machine:

| Channel | Best for | Platforms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homebrew | macOS/Linux workstations; managed upgrades | macOS/Linux amd64 and arm64 |
| npm (public registry) | Node toolchains, workstations, and public CI | macOS/Linux x64 and arm64; Windows x64 |
| npm (GitHub Packages) | Organization CI that already uses GitHub Packages | macOS/Linux x64 and arm64; Windows x64 |
| Release archive | Air-gapped hosts, exact-version pinning, Windows | macOS/Linux amd64 and arm64; Windows amd64 |
| Linux package | Fleet management with `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.apk` | amd64 and arm64 |

## Homebrew (macOS and Linux)

Use Homebrew when you want the shortest path and automatic upgrades alongside
your other tooling.

```sh
brew install --cask aziron-ai/atlas/atlas
atlas version
```

Homebrew names fully qualified casks as `<owner>/<tap>/<cask>`. The repository
`aziron-ai/homebrew-atlas` becomes the tap `aziron-ai/atlas`; the cask and the
installed executable are both named `atlas`.

## npm (public registry)

Use npm when Atlas should install through an existing Node toolchain or CI
pipeline. The public package needs no registry configuration or GitHub token:

```sh
npm install -g @aziron/atlas
atlas version
```

Pin an exact version for reproducible environments:

```sh
npm install -g @aziron/atlas@0.1.54
```

### Installing a Binary You Already Have

Offline, behind a TLS-intercepting proxy, or with a binary you built or
verified yourself, point `ATLAS_BINARY` at it:

```sh
ATLAS_BINARY=/absolute/path/to/atlas npm install -g @aziron/atlas
```

**Since 0.1.55** postinstall honours it. It checks that the path exists, is
a file, is executable, and that `atlas version` prints an Atlas version line
within 30 seconds, then copies the binary into the package, replacing any
earlier copy. It makes no request to the release host and never falls back to
a download: an invalid path fails the install with a message that names the
problem. A relative path resolves against the directory you ran `npm` from.
`ATLAS_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1` makes postinstall do nothing and takes precedence over
`ATLAS_BINARY`. `checksums.txt` covers the release archives, not a binary you
supply, so verify that binary yourself
([#151](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/151)).

### GitHub Packages alternative

Atlas is also published to GitHub Packages as `@aziron-ai/atlas`. Use this
coordinate when organization CI already authenticates to GitHub Packages.
Point the `@aziron-ai` scope at GitHub and use a token with `read:packages`:

```sh
npm config set @aziron-ai:registry https://npm.pkg.github.com
npm config set //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN
npm install -g @aziron-ai/atlas
atlas version
```

```sh
npm install -g @aziron-ai/atlas@0.1.54
```

Both npm coordinates install the same wrapper and native Atlas binary for the
current platform. If you do not need npm specifically, Homebrew is the simpler
path on macOS and Linux.

## Release Archives

Use a release archive when no package manager is available, on air-gapped
hosts, or when you need to pin and checksum exact bytes. Choose the current
version and platform from
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/releases/latest):

```sh
VERSION=0.1.54
OS=darwin       # darwin or linux
ARCH=arm64      # arm64 or amd64
ASSET="atlas_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
BASE="https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/releases/download/v${VERSION}"

curl -fLO "$BASE/$ASSET"
curl -fLO "$BASE/checksums.txt"
grep " $ASSET\$" checksums.txt | shasum -a 256 -c -
tar -xzf "$ASSET"
sudo install -m 0755 atlas /usr/local/bin/atlas
atlas version
```

On Linux, replace the checksum command with `sha256sum -c -` when available.

### Windows

Each release also includes a Windows amd64 archive. Download it from the same
release page, extract the `atlas.exe` executable, and add its directory to
`PATH`. Alternatively, the npm channel above supports Windows x64.

## Native Linux Packages

Use native packages when your fleet is managed through a distribution package
manager. Each release includes `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.apk` packages for amd64
and arm64. Download the matching package from the release page, then install:

```sh
# Debian or Ubuntu
sudo dpkg -i atlas_0.1.54_linux_amd64.deb

# Fedora or RHEL
sudo rpm -U atlas_0.1.54_linux_amd64.rpm

# Alpine
sudo apk add --allow-untrusted atlas_0.1.54_linux_amd64.apk
```

## Post-Install: Assistant Bootstrap

Homebrew and npm installations run `atlas bootstrap` after install. Bootstrap
registers Atlas as an MCP server and installs the atlas-first skill and
CLAUDE.md directive for every detected assistant (Claude desktop and CLI,
Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini). It is idempotent — safe to run repeatedly
and from a package post-install hook. Inspect the proposed changes at any
time without writing anything:

```sh
atlas bootstrap --dry-run
```

To prevent the npm post-install bootstrap in managed environments:

```sh
ATLAS_SKIP_BOOTSTRAP=1 npm install -g @aziron/atlas
```

Archive and Linux-package installs do not configure assistants automatically;
run `atlas bootstrap` yourself when you want them connected.

## PATH Note

Assistants launch Atlas by resolving `atlas` from `PATH`, so the binary must
be reachable from a login shell — not only your current session. Homebrew and
the Linux packages handle this; for archives, `/usr/local/bin` (used above)
is on `PATH` by default on most systems. For npm installs, ensure npm's
global bin directory is on `PATH`.

## Verify the Installation

Verification confirms three distinct things: the binary is on `PATH`, it
runs, and it is the same binary your assistants will launch.

```sh
command -v atlas
atlas version
atlas doctor --verify atlas
```

`atlas doctor` reports upgrade health and schema/index contract state;
`--verify atlas` additionally checks for binary drift — whether the `atlas`
on `PATH` (what assistants launch via `command:"atlas"`) matches the running
binary. Drift typically means an old install shadows the new one earlier on
`PATH`.

Continue with [Getting Started](getting-started), or read
[Core Concepts](concepts) for the model behind the commands.

---

# Core Concepts
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/concepts/

# Core Concepts

Every Atlas command shares the same underlying model: a local knowledge graph
of your code, a snapshot timeline over its history, one workspace-resolution
scheme, and one set of output controls. Understanding these once makes the
whole [CLI Reference](cli) predictable.

## The Knowledge Graph

Atlas answers structural questions from a **knowledge graph** rather than
text search, so results are exact relationships, not pattern matches. The
graph is built by `atlas index`, which parses a repository into:

- **Symbols** — functions, methods, classes, and other definitions.
- **Call edges** — who calls whom, powering `callers`, `path`, `impact`, and
  the graph-shape commands (`hubs`, `communities`).
- **Routes** — the HTTP routes a repository serves and calls, powering
  cross-repo queries such as `consumers` and `dependencies`.
- **Coverage** — test-to-symbol links, from static call-graph reachability or
  an imported runtime profile (`atlas coverage import`).

Alongside the graph, indexing persists a lexical (BM25 + trigram) search
index. Everything lives in an embedded SQLite database, by default
`sqlite://./.atlas/atlas.db` inside the repository — no daemon or service is
required to query it.

```sh
atlas index .
```

## Snapshots and History

Each indexed commit becomes a **snapshot**, giving the graph a per-commit
timeline — you can ask not only what the code looks like, but how its
structure changed. `atlas history` lists the timeline; `atlas snapshot-diff`
computes a structural diff (symbols and edges added, removed, modified)
between two snapshots, defaulting to the latest snapshot and the one before
it. Both `--from` and `--to` accept a commit sha (prefix ok) or snapshot id.

```sh
atlas snapshot-diff --from a1b2c3d --to HEAD
```

## Workspace Resolution

Every command needs to know which repository and which database it is
operating on; three global flags resolve that, and the defaults make the
common case zero-config.

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--repo` | Repo workspace: a path, `org/name`, or `repo_id`; `'*'` = all repos on `search`/`semantic-search` | the current directory |
| `--db` | Storage DSN: `sqlite://PATH` or `postgres://...` | `sqlite://./.atlas/atlas.db` |
| `--tenant` | Tenant/org scope to isolate repos to (hosted multi-tenant) | empty = all repos |

Run from inside an indexed repository and no flags are needed. Point `--db`
at a shared database to query many repositories from one place:

```sh
atlas search "rate limiter" --repo '*' --db sqlite:///srv/atlas/atlas.db
```

## Output Control

Output has two independent axes — shape and depth — so you can tune results
for a terminal, a script, or an LLM context window.

| Flag | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format` | `plain` \| `json` \| `compact` \| `ndjson` — output shape | `json` |
| `--json` | shorthand for `--format json` | — |
| `--detail` | `low` \| `medium` \| `high` \| `xhigh` — graph context per item | `high` |

Retrieval operations (`callers`, `refs`, `impact`) floor at `high` detail so
they never silently drop the context they exist to provide; `xhigh` opts into
cross-repo context. For agents, prefer `--format plain`: it carries the same
answer in far fewer tokens than structured JSON, which matters when every
query result lands in a model's context window.

```sh
atlas search "session store" --format plain --detail low
```

## Three Surfaces

The same graph is exposed three ways, so humans, services, and AI agents each
get a native interface without separate infrastructure.

- **CLI** — the commands in this documentation; scriptable via `--format`.
- **REST HTTP API** — `atlas serve` runs the HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:3099` by
  default (use `--addr 0.0.0.0:3099` to expose it) and hosts the dashboard at that
  URL (pass `--open` to auto-open it in your browser); `--mcp` also mounts MCP over HTTP at `POST /mcp`.
  The dashboard includes the [Ask Workbench](workbench): a conversation about the
  codebase where Atlas gathers cited evidence and a model you choose writes the answer.
- **MCP** — `atlas mcp` exposes graph, search, and impact as MCP tools to LLM
  agents over stdio by default, with `--http`/`--sse` transports available.
  Both `serve` and `mcp` keep the graph fresh with a background repo watch
  (`--watch`, on by default; disable with `--watch=false` or
  `ATLAS_NO_WATCH=1`). [Getting Started](getting-started) covers wiring
  assistants via `atlas bootstrap`; [MCP Tools](mcp) covers the tool surface.

```sh
atlas serve --mcp
```

## Read-Only Mode

Use `--read-only` when the database must not change — CI caches,
content-addressed artifacts, shared read replicas. It opens the database
immutably: no migration runs, no WAL/journal files are created, and no
`telemetry.db` appears next to it — artifact bytes hash identically after any
query. A missing database errors instead of being created. If you still want
telemetry in this mode, point `--telemetry-db` at an explicit writable path.

```sh
atlas symbol NewServer --read-only
```

## Local-First vs Hosted

Atlas is local by default: indexing, querying, serving, and MCP all run
against your local database, and nothing leaves the machine. Two commands opt
into a central Atlas server, and only for fleet telemetry and org skills:

- `atlas connect` registers the machine with a central server under a stable
  device identity and installs capture hooks. What leaves the machine is
  governed by the data level (`--level`): `off`, `telemetry` (metrics only),
  `interactions` (normalized prompts + redacted traces; the default), or
  `full` (raw prompts; org opt-in). Raw transcripts, tool outputs, answers,
  and secrets never leave the machine at any level. `atlas disconnect`
  reverses it.
- `atlas sync` is the fleet telemetry uplink — `sync status` shows the
  configuration, kill switches, and per-stream cursors; `sync now` pushes
  pending telemetry once.

Connected machines can also exchange org-trusted skills and automations
(`atlas skill push/pull`, `atlas recall push/pull`). Everything else —
`index`, `search`, `callers`, `impact`, `serve`, `mcp` — works with no server
and no account. On a hosted multi-tenant server, `--tenant` scopes queries to
one org. See [Configuration](configuration) for the related knobs.

```sh
atlas sync status
```

---

# The Dashboard
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/dashboard/

# The dashboard

The dashboard is the browser view of everything one Atlas service holds: the
repositories it indexed, the graph inside them, the questions it answered and
the tools it is connected to. Every view shares one frame — a navigation rail
on the left, a search box in the header and a symbol inspector that opens over
any page. Reach for it when you want to look around a codebase instead of
asking the command line one question at a time.

## Open It

Start the service and open the dashboard in a browser:

```sh
atlas serve
# then open http://127.0.0.1:3099/dashboard
```

The first page is the **Command Center** (`#/overview`). Every view has its
own hash route — `#/map`, `#/ask`, `#/orient` — so a link to a view, a symbol
or a question can be pasted into chat and opens the same page for the next
reader. [Dashboard and API](service) covers the service flags, tokens and the
address it binds to.

![The Command Center: KPI tiles, the Observe row, Ready to automate, Connector pulse, Skills lifecycle and the Live activity rail](assets/docs/dashboard/command-center.png "The Command Center on a service that has indexed inference-gateway and has Prometheus and a log pull configured.")

## Find Your Way Around

The rail on the left groups the views by job. A badge beside an item is a live
count: events in the stream, open incidents, firing alerts, skills,
repositories.

![The lower half of the navigation rail: the OBSERVE, AUTOMATE, FLEET, CODEBASE and SYSTEM groups with their badges](assets/docs/dashboard/nav-rail-lower.png "The lower half of the rail (COMMAND and EXPLORE are in the screenshot above). OBSERVE appears only once a monitoring tool is configured; Builds and Traces are greyed until Jenkins and Tempo are.")

| Group | Views | Use it to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **COMMAND** | Command Center, Live Activity | See what the service holds and what it is doing right now. |
| **PINNED** | Symbols you starred | Jump back to the symbols you keep returning to. Hidden until you pin one. |
| **EXPLORE** | Ask Atlas, Ask Workbench, Code Map, Orientation, Resolve, Files, Routes, Impact, Path Finder, Changes | Read and question the code: search, ask, map, trace a path, size a change. |
| **OBSERVE** | Log Streams, What Changed, Alerts & Metrics, Builds, Incidents, Traces | Read what a running system is doing. Each item is greyed until the tool it needs (Loki or Elasticsearch, Prometheus, Jenkins, Tempo) is configured. |
| **AUTOMATE** | Skill Studio, Skills, Approvals | Turn repeated work into reviewed skills and decide pending requests. |
| **FLEET** | Devices, Connectors | See connected machines and configure monitoring tools. |
| **CODEBASE** | Workspace, Hot Symbols, Freshness | List every indexed repository, its most-connected symbols and how fresh each index is. |
| **SYSTEM** | System | Check the service's own health, settings and AI providers. |

The header carries four controls on the right:

![Header controls: the search box with its / shortcut, the Live toggle, the ? button and the theme button](assets/docs/dashboard/header-controls.png "Search, Live, tour replay and theme.")

- **Search symbols, routes…** — the omnibox. Press `/` anywhere to focus it
  (see below).
- **Live** — pauses and resumes the dashboard's live refresh. Pause it when
  you want the numbers on screen to stop moving.
- **?** — replays the five-step product tour: Orientation, Ask Atlas, Code
  Map, Routes, and search with the command palette. Each step highlights the
  real control; **Skip** closes it, **Back** and **Next** step through.
- The **theme** button switches between dark and light. The choice is
  remembered in this browser.

![The first step of the product tour, highlighting Orientation in the rail](assets/docs/dashboard/product-tour.png "The tour's first step, opened from the ? button.")

## Read the Command Center

The Command Center is a summary of the whole service, read from one endpoint
(`/api/v1/dashboard`). Nothing on it is sample data: a tile with nothing to
count says so. Click a tile to open the view that owns its number.

![The six KPI tiles of the Command Center](assets/docs/dashboard/kpi-strip.png "The KPI strip.")

| Tile | The number | Opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tokens saved (recall)** | Tokens the recall ledger recorded as saved by replaying a stored answer, with the number of replay runs beneath. | Skills |
| **Hit rate** | Cache and shadow hits over recorded turns. | Skills |
| **Fleet devices** | Machines connected with `atlas connect`; a device is flagged stale after seven days without a push. | Devices |
| **Active skills** | Trusted skills, with the candidate and validating counts beneath. | Skills |
| **Events/min** | Recorded events over the last ten minutes. | Live Activity |
| **System** | The service's p95 serving latency and its uptime. | System |

Below the tiles:

- **OBSERVE** — one tile per configured monitoring tool, such as **Log
  pulls**, **Open incidents** and **Firing alerts**. With nothing configured
  the row reads **Observe is off** and lists each tool, the views it unlocks,
  and the CLI command and HTTP route that configure it.
- **Ready to automate** — repeated procedures mined from real sessions,
  ranked by projected savings, each with **Create skill**. Empty until agents
  work through Atlas with episode capture on.
- **Connector pulse** — events per connector in the live window.
- **Skills lifecycle** — skills per stage: candidate, validating, trusted,
  quarantined, revoked.
- **Code graph index** — **Indexed symbols**, **Repos indexed**, **Indexed
  edges** and **Route records**: the stored rows of each indexed repository's
  latest snapshot, summed over the repositories, the same totals the
  Workspace view shows. Since 0.1.55 both views share one calculation, each
  tile reads "—" until the first dashboard frame arrives (an empty index shows
  a measured 0), hovering a tile names that scope, and **Graph edges** is
  renamed **Indexed edges** because it counts stored edge rows, not the
  graph's resolved edges ([#158](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/158)). The card links to **Orientation** and
  **Hot Symbols**.
- **Live activity** (right rail) — the seven newest events: what was asked,
  which connector, how many tokens, how long it took. **All** opens the full
  stream. Below it, an **Approvals** card appears when requests await a
  decision, and a **Devices** card lists connected machines.

**Live Activity** (`#/events`) is the full stream. Filter it by connector with
the chips (each shows its count), by tier (**automation**, **exact**,
**semantic**, **live**), or by any text in the **Filter events…** box.

![Live Activity filtered to the atlas connector, showing three indexing events](assets/docs/dashboard/live-activity.png "Live Activity filtered to the atlas connector: each row is an indexing pass with its file, symbol, edge and route counts.")

## Search and Inspect a Symbol

The omnibox in the header finds any indexed symbol from any view.

1. Press `/` (or click the box) and type at least two characters.
2. Results arrive grouped by kind — **METHOD**, **FUNCTION**, **TYPE**,
   **FIELD**, **KEY** — each with its file and line.
3. Use `↑` `↓` to select and `Enter` to open the symbol in the inspector.
   `Enter` with nothing selected sends the text to **Ask Atlas** as a question
   instead (or, when logs are configured, a query that looks like a log line
   to **Log Streams**).

![Typing modelDenied into the header search, selecting the method and opening the inspector](assets/docs/dashboard/omnibox-search.mp4 "Search for modelDenied and open it in the inspector.")

The inspector docks on the right, over whatever view you are on. For
`modelDenied` it shows:

- the name, kind and location (`routes.go:622`), with a star to pin it, a
  copy-link button and close;
- **Code Map** and **Ask about this**, which open the symbol in those views;
- **Explain** — the signature; then **Body excerpt**, **Callers** (5),
  **References** (5) and **Neighbors**, each loaded on its own and each saying
  so when it is empty;
- **Blast radius** and **History** at the foot, which run the impact and
  history queries for this symbol.

![The symbol inspector open on modelDenied, listing five callers and five references](assets/docs/dashboard/inspector.png "The inspector on modelDenied: five callers, all in api/routes.go.")

The inspector's state rides the URL
(`?sym=modelDenied&symPath=api/routes.go`), so a copied link reopens it. Star
a symbol and it appears under **PINNED** in the rail; click the pin to reopen
the inspector. Pins are kept per store in this browser, up to 20.

![The PINNED group in the rail holding modelDenied](assets/docs/dashboard/pinned-symbol.png "A pinned symbol in the rail.")

For actions as well as symbols, press `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K`) for the command palette.
It jumps to any view by name, lists matching symbols, and offers actions built
on your text: **Ask Atlas**, **Search Routes**, **Impact** for the top hit,
**Path Finder** from the top hit.

![The command palette with modelDenied typed: symbol rows and four actions](assets/docs/dashboard/command-palette.png "The command palette: symbol rows are live index hits; the actions start a view pre-filled.")

## Get Oriented in a Repository

**Orientation** (`#/orient`) is the page to open first on an unfamiliar
repository. Pick the repository at the top; **Open Code Map** and **Ask
Atlas** carry it into those views.

![Orientation for inference-gateway: graph counts, language bars, entry points and load-bearing symbols](assets/docs/dashboard/orientation.png "Orientation for inference-gateway.")

- The counts strip — **FILES**, **SYMBOLS**, **EDGES**, **COMMUNITIES**,
  **ISOLATED** — and a bar per language come from the graph report, which
  reads non-test code symbols and call edges. That is why they are smaller
  than the repository's stored totals: 89 files and 3,526 symbols here,
  against 307 files and 11,092 symbols stored.
- **Entry points** lists the routes the repository serves — method, path,
  handler — with the confidence of each match.
- **Load-bearing symbols** ranks the hubs by degree; **Inspect** opens one in
  the inspector, **Map** in the Code Map.
- **Modules & communities**, further down, groups symbols that call each
  other densely.

## Browse Repositories and Files

**Workspace** (`#/workspace`, under CODEBASE) lists every repository the
service holds. The tiles total repositories, files, symbols, dependency edges
and route contracts; the **Knowledge map** draws one tile per repository,
sized by symbols and coloured by how recently it was indexed. The
**Per-repository index** table below gives each repository's counts, index
mode, age and status, with **Orient me** and **Map** buttons.

![Workspace: totals, the knowledge map and the per-repository table header](assets/docs/dashboard/workspace.png "Workspace on the demo service: inference-gateway plus two connected sources indexed as virtual repositories.")

**Files** (`#/files`) walks a repository as a tree. Sort the tree by
**name**, **syms** or **rel**, or filter it by path and symbol name. Select a
file and the **Details** panel shows its relations, the routes it serves, a
likely test file, the packages it imports and the files that import it, with
**Map this file's folder**, **Ask about this file** and **Compare…**.

![Files: api/routes.go selected, showing 882 relations and the nine routes it serves](assets/docs/dashboard/files.png "api/routes.go in Files: 882 relations and nine served routes, each with its handler.")

## Check the Service

**System** (`#/system`) has two tabs. **Overview** is the service's own
footprint, streamed live: uptime, memory, CPU, serving latency, the size of
the graph database, the lexical index and the telemetry database, events
recorded and an estimate of tokens served. Below the tiles are a live resource
timeline, a **Per-tool breakdown** of every tool call served, and the
operational settings with where each value comes from (environment, settings
file or default). **Run self-diagnostic**, **Clear stale snapshots** and
**Compact storage** are the maintenance actions.

![System overview: runtime tiles for uptime, memory, CPU, latency and storage](assets/docs/dashboard/system-runtime.png "System → Overview.")

**App integrations** is where the optional AI answer gets its provider. Atlas
detects the Claude and Codex CLIs and API keys on the machine; each provider
card shows its model, the credential it uses, what leaves the machine, and a
**Test** button. The same tab shows the GitHub and Pulse integrations of the
Ask Workbench and the Jira sign-in.

![System → App integrations: the AI providers card with Claude as the default, detected and ready](assets/docs/dashboard/system-ai-providers.png "App integrations: Claude detected and ready as the default provider.")

## From the CLI

The same facts the frame shows are one command away. `atlas status` is the
storage and contract check, one line per repository:

```sh
atlas status --format plain
status  schema 8  index_format 5  lexical 4  mcp 2  driver sqlite
  inference-gateway  52496750  format 5  symbols 11092  edges 13900
```

`atlas stats` is one repository's index telemetry. `store_rows` are the stored
totals the Workspace view shows; `graph` is the report's non-test call graph
that Orientation shows:

```sh
atlas stats --format plain
stats inference-gateway  local/sqlite  history 1  coverage_facts 0
  latest 52496750  mode full  files 307  symbols 11092  edges 13900  routes 71  53534ms
  store_rows files 307  symbols 11092  edges 13900  routes 71
  graph files 89  symbols 3526  edges 1317  communities 3161  isolated 3121
  langs  go:3511 bash:9 typescript:6
```

`atlas repo list` is the Workspace table; `atlas repo rm` forgets a
repository and its data:

```sh
atlas repo list --format plain
NAME               PATH               COMMIT                                    INDEXED               STATUS
inference-gateway  inference-gateway  524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a  2026-10-28T05:16:55Z  ready
```

Every command and flag is in the [CLI reference](cli).

## From the API

The Command Center reads one snapshot, `GET /api/v1/dashboard`, and keeps it
fresh over `GET /api/v1/dashboard/stream` (server-sent events). The snapshot's
top-level blocks are `meta`, `kpis`, `series`, `tierBreakdown`, `clusters`,
`automations`, `approvals`, `events`, `repoObservability`, `devices`,
`decisions`, `recall`, `system` and `observe`; Workspace reads
`repoObservability`. `GET /api/v1/status` is the same check as `atlas status`:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3099/api/v1/status
{"data":{"tier":"local","storage_driver":"sqlite","vector_backend":"disabled","repos_indexed":1,
 "repos":[{"repo_full_name":"inference-gateway","commit_sha":"524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
  "files":307,"symbols":11092,"edges":13900,"routes":71,"producer_routes":39,"consumer_calls":32,
  "indexed_at":"2026-10-28T05:16:55Z","state":"ready", …}]}}
```

Tokens, the full route list and the HTTP MCP endpoint are on
[Dashboard and API](service).

# Code Map and Graph
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/code-map/

# Code Map and graph

The Code Map draws the stored call graph of a repository: which folders hold
what, which symbols call which, and how one function reaches another.
Everything on it is an edge the index recorded — calls, references, imports —
never a guess. Reach for it when you need to see the shape around a symbol
before you change it, or to find your way into a folder you have never opened.

## Open It

Choose **Code Map** under EXPLORE, or open `#/map`. With no symbol chosen the
map opens in the **Clusters** lens: the whole repository packed as its real
folder tree.

![The Code Map in the Clusters lens for inference-gateway: folders packed as circles with edges between them](assets/docs/code-map/map-clusters.png "inference-gateway in Clusters: internal, providers, tests, api and the rest, sized by the symbols inside.")

The controls along the top are shared by every lens:

![The repository picker, the five lens buttons, the edge-kind chips and the find / seed box](assets/docs/code-map/map-controls.png "Repository, lens, edge kinds with their counts, and the find / seed box.")

- The **repository** picker.
- The lens buttons: **Flow**, **Clusters**, **Explorer**, **Workbench** (beta)
  and **Repos**.
- The edge-kind chips with their counts — **calls 2,383**, **references
  2,181**, **imports 929** on inference-gateway. Click a chip to hide or show
  that kind. Imports start off in Flow and Explorer, which read call flow, and
  on in Clusters and Workbench, which read architecture.
- **find / seed a symbol…** — type a name to light up matches on the canvas
  (`Enter` cycles through them) or pick a row to re-root the map on it.

The line under the controls counts what is drawn against what exists —
`0 of 3,430 symbols · 318 of 5,493 edges — 28 folders collapsed` — so a
hidden part of the graph is always named. **⧉ link** copies a link that
carries the lens, the focus, pins and edge kinds; **ⓘ** explains why the
current lens looks the way it does.

## Pick a Lens

The five lenses are five ways of reading the same stored graph. The focus
symbol rides the URL, so switching lens keeps your place.

| Lens | What it shows | Reach for it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Flow** | One symbol at a time: callers enter from the left, callees leave on the right, one to three layers deep. | You are about to change a function and want to see who feeds it and what it calls. |
| **Clusters** | The whole repository as its folder tree, packed in circles, with the edges between folders aggregated and counted. Same input, same picture. | You are new to a repository, or want to see which folders lean on which. |
| **Explorer** | An answer-first list of one symbol's callers and dependencies, with call-site evidence in each row and a small synced map (25 nodes at most). | You want the exact list, with line numbers, rather than a picture. |
| **Workbench** (beta) | An interactive canvas of modules, collapsed to badges on a large repository, with style, filter and layout panels, box select and PNG export. | You want to arrange and export a picture of part of the graph. |
| **Repos** | The dependency graph between repositories, from HTTP calls one repository makes that match a route another serves. | Several services are indexed and you need to know which calls which. |

![Flow lens focused on modelDenied: five callers on the left, seven callees on the right](assets/docs/code-map/map-flow.png "Flow on modelDenied at depth 2: five first-degree callers, seven first-degree callees, and the next layer on each side.")

![Explorer lens on modelDenied: the focus card, callers grouped by file, dependencies grouped by module, and a small synced map](assets/docs/code-map/map-explorer.png "Explorer on modelDenied: 5 callers, 7 dependencies, 5 call sites — each row expands to its evidence.")

![Workbench beta lens: modules collapsed to badges, with style, module and symbol-kind panels on the left](assets/docs/code-map/map-workbench.png "Workbench (beta): 117 modules collapsed to badges; tick a module to expand it on the canvas.")

Workbench is a beta: the first time you choose it, the map explains that it
loads an extra analysis engine once and asks you to confirm with **Enable
Workbench**. **Repos** needs at least two repositories where one calls the
other over HTTP; with nothing to join it says so:

![Repos lens: a repo-pair matrix of zeros and the note that no cross-repo route join is recorded](assets/docs/code-map/map-repos.png "Repos on the demo service: inference-gateway calls no route another indexed repository serves, so the matrix is empty.")

## Read the Legend and Filter Edges

Each lens has a **Legend** in the lower left of the canvas; click its title to
fold it away. In Clusters it names the colour of each top folder, the line
style of each edge kind, and how to read size: a folder's size is the number
of symbols inside it, a symbol's size is its degree. Open top folders carry
`↓` fan-in and `↑` fan-out badges.

![The Clusters legend: folder colours, edge kinds and the size rules](assets/docs/code-map/map-legend.png "The Clusters legend.")

The Clusters toolbar controls how much is drawn:

![The Clusters toolbar: tint, EDGES all / focus-only / off, link, the lens note and the count strip](assets/docs/code-map/map-modebar.png "tint, the EDGES switch, link and the count strip.")

- **EDGES all** draws every edge between folders; past the edge budget they
  bundle into weighted ribbons.
- **focus-only** draws edges only for what you hover or select — the calm way
  to read a busy repository.
- **off** draws no edges: folders only.
- **tint** colours open folders in their hue.

To zoom, use the **+** and **−** buttons in the lower right of the canvas or
the mouse wheel; drag to pan; **⤢** (or `0`) fits the drawing to the frame.
Click a node to select it.

## Seed a Symbol and Read Its Neighbourhood

Flow and Explorer read one symbol at a time, so they start by asking for one.

1. Click **Flow**. With no focus yet, the lens shows a search box and the
   repository's top hubs by degree.
2. Type a name — `modelDenied` — and click the row for the definition you
   mean (`api/routes.go:622`).
3. Read the layers: the five handlers that call `modelDenied` on the left,
   what it calls on the right (`ModelMatches`, `ParseModelSet`, the logger's
   `Error`), the second layer beyond each. Edge width grows with the number of
   call sites.

![Switching to Flow, searching modelDenied, picking it, and the layered call flow drawing around it](assets/docs/code-map/seed-symbol.mp4 "Seed Flow with modelDenied and read its callers and callees.")

The Flow toolbar works on the focus:

- **− 2 +** steps the depth between 1 and 3; each step is a fresh query.
- **Hubs ▾** lists the repository's hubs to re-seed from.
- **×N** merges same-name definitions within a layer into one chip, such as
  **Error ×4**.
- **Path A→B** draws the path between two symbols on the canvas; **Impact**
  overlays the blast radius of the selected symbol; **Neighbors** fetches and
  grafts the selected symbol's neighbours that are not drawn yet.
- When a layer holds many symbols that call the same thing, they fold into a
  **co-callers** bar; click it to expand.

Anywhere on the map, double-click a symbol to re-root Flow on it. Explorer
reads the same focus as a list: the focus card counts callers, dependencies,
call sites and modules, and each row expands to the call-site lines.

## Isolate a Folder

A large folder can be read on its own. In Clusters, double-click the folder:
the map redraws with only that subtree, a breadcrumb
(`inference-gateway › providers`) shows where you are, and the count strip
says `isolated to providers`. **⤴ leave isolate** returns to the whole
repository.

![Clusters isolated to the providers folder: types, registry, routing, transformers, constants, core and client](assets/docs/code-map/map-isolate.png "providers isolated: 1,172 symbols, with common_types.go holding 873 of them.")

## Find the Path Between Two Symbols

**Path Finder** (`#/path`) answers "how does A reach B?" with the shortest
forward chain of stored call edges, or says that none exists.

1. Pick the repository and a depth budget (6 by default).
2. In **From (the caller side)** search and pick the start symbol; in **To
   (the callee side)** pick the target.
3. Read the chain: one card per step with kind, signature and location, and
   the edge between steps. The map button on a card opens that symbol in the
   Code Map.

![Path Finder: ChatCompletionsHandler reaches ModelMatches in two hops through modelDenied](assets/docs/code-map/path-finder.png "ChatCompletionsHandler reaches ModelMatches in 2 hops, through modelDenied.")

Call edges have a direction. If no path is found, **swap** asks the reverse
question in one click. **Copy link to this chain** gives a link that reopens
the same answer.

## Resolve a Log Line to Code

**Resolve** (`#/resolve`) starts from the other end: paste a log line, a stack
frame or an error string, one per line, and Atlas finds the statement that
emits it, then walks its blast radius and the recent change window. At index
time Atlas records the message each log statement can emit, so a line with
different ids, timestamps and values still matches.

1. Pick the repository.
2. Paste the line — here a JSON log line from the gateway:
   `{"level":"error",…,"msg":"model not in allowed list","model":"gpt-4o",…}`.
3. Click **Resolve**. The answer is a chain of three cards.

![Resolve: the log line matched to modelDenied at routes.go:625, its impact, and the change window](assets/docs/code-map/resolve.png "The line resolves to modelDenied (routes.go:625, 100% match, exact_skeleton); changing it would touch seven handlers.")

- **Match** — the emitting symbol and line, the match score and the reason
  the server gives (`exact_skeleton`), with **Inspect** and **Map**.
- **Impact** — the symbols a change to it would reach.
- **Change window** — the snapshot timeline and what changed between the last
  two snapshots. With a single snapshot indexed, it says a diff needs two.

The commit and snapshot the evidence came from are pinned at the top of the
answer.

## From the CLI

Each map question has a command. Output below is from inference-gateway, in
`--format plain`.

`atlas neighbors` — a symbol's direct callers and callees (what Flow draws at
depth 1):

```sh
atlas neighbors modelDenied --format plain
neighbors modelDenied  callers 5  callees 6
  callers(5)  ChatCompletionsHandler, ImagesHandler, MessagesHandler, ResponsesHandler, handleImagesMultipart
  callees(6)  Error, Error, ModelMatches, ParseModelSet, Error, Error
```

`atlas path` — the shortest forward call path (Path Finder); `--max-depth`
sets the budget:

```sh
atlas path ChatCompletionsHandler ModelMatches --format plain
path ChatCompletionsHandler -> ModelMatches  len 2
  steps  ChatCompletionsHandler -> modelDenied -> ModelMatches

atlas path main ModelMatches --format plain
path main -> ModelMatches  NOT FOUND
```

`atlas hubs` and `atlas communities` — the load-bearing symbols and the dense
clusters (Orientation's lists):

```sh
atlas hubs --limit 5 --format plain
hubs  total 5
  main  function  in 0  out 71  total 71  cmd/gateway/main.go
  ProviderImpl.ListModels  method  in 2  out 53  total 55  providers/core/provider.go
  RouterImpl.handleImagesMultipart  method  in 2  out 53  total 55  api/routes.go
  RouterImpl.MessagesHandler  method  in 0  out 52  total 52  api/routes.go
  RouterImpl.ImagesHandler  method  in 0  out 51  total 51  api/routes.go

atlas communities --limit 3 --format plain
communities  total 3161  shown 3
  #0  size 137  ProviderImpl.ListModels, RouterImpl.handleImagesMultipart, RouterImpl.MessagesHandler
  #1  size 69  main, LoggerZapImpl.Debug, MockLogger.Debug
  #2  size 65  LoggerZapImpl.Error, MockLogger.Error, MockLoggerMockRecorder.Error
```

`atlas report` — summary, hubs and communities in one Markdown report:

```sh
atlas report --format plain
# Graph report

## Summary

- Files: 89
- Symbols (nodes): 3526
- Call edges: 1317
- Communities (size > 1): 40
- Isolated nodes: 3121
- Languages: go:3511 bash:9 typescript:6
- Edge kinds: calls:4706 references:3158 imports:540
…
```

`atlas export` — a symbol's neighbourhood or the whole graph as `json`,
`mermaid`, `dot` or a self-contained `html` page; `--bundle DIR` writes the
interactive page and the report together:

```sh
atlas export --symbol modelDenied --depth 1 --format mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0["RouterImpl (type)"]
  n1["modelDenied (method)"]
  n2["ChatCompletionsHandler (method)"]
  …
  n9["ParseModelSet (function)"]
  n10["ModelMatches (function)"]
  n2 --> n1
  n1 --> n10
  n1 --> n9
  …
```

Pasting a log line works from the terminal too: `atlas logsites resolve "<line>"`
returns the same match (`api/routes.go:625`, `modelDenied`, `exact_skeleton`).
Flags for each command are in the [CLI reference](cli); the map reads
`GET /api/v1/export`, Path Finder `GET /api/v1/path` and Resolve
`POST /api/v1/resolve` (see [Dashboard and API](service)).

- [The dashboard](dashboard) — the frame, the omnibox and the inspector.
- [Search and Ask](search-and-ask) — find a symbol by name or ask in plain
  language.
- [Impact and review](impact) — the full blast radius of a change.
- [Change lens and history](history) — what each indexing pass changed.
- [Observe](observe) — log streams and incidents that Resolve links back to
  code.

# Search and Ask
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/search-and-ask/

# Search and Ask

Search finds a symbol, a file or a phrase when you know some of its words. Ask
answers a question in plain language with the lines of code that answer it,
quoted and cited — and, if you turn it on, a short AI-written answer built
only from those lines. Use search when you are looking for a thing; use Ask
when you are looking for an explanation.

## Open It

Search lives in two places: the header box of the dashboard (**Search
symbols, routes…**, shortcut `/`) and `atlas search` on the command line. Ask
is **Ask Atlas** under EXPLORE, at `#/ask`.

![The Ask Atlas page before a question: the question box, corpus switch, repository picker, Synthesize with AI, the model picker, Recent questions and Suggested](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-page.png "Ask Atlas, ready for a question. Suggested questions are templates over the repository's real hubs.")

## Search for a Symbol

Type at least two characters into the header box. Atlas returns the matching
definitions grouped by kind, each with its file and line; `Enter` opens the
selected one in the inspector ([The dashboard](dashboard) shows the whole
flow).

![Header search for ModelMatches: FUNCTION, TYPE and FIELD groups with file locations](assets/docs/search-and-ask/omnibox-results.png "ModelMatches in the header search: the function first, then related functions, types and fields.")

Search is **code-aware lexical search**. In practice that means:

- **It reads code names the way you type them.** Identifiers are split on
  camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, dots and slashes, and every piece is
  indexed beside the whole name. `allowedmodels` finds the `ALLOWED_MODELS`
  keys; `user` finds `GetUserByID`.
- **It ranks by BM25.** A result where your words are rare and concentrated —
  in the name, the signature, the doc comment or the path — ranks above one
  where they are common and scattered.
- **It forgives small typos.** Trigram matching compares three-letter
  fragments, so `modlDenied` still finds `modelDenied`.
- **It searches paths too.** `model_filter.go` or `providers/routing` name a
  file or folder; a path-shaped query ranks the file whose path is exactly
  that first.
- **Ties have one order.** Since 0.1.55, results with equal scores come back
  by path, then name, kind, signature and line, so two fresh indexes of the
  same commit, at any worker count, return the same page in the same order
  ([#135](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/135)).

Results carry a kind: `function`, `method`, `method_spec` (an interface
method), `type`, `field`, `constant`, `key` (a configuration or YAML key), and,
from documentation, `section` and `document`. Filter with `--kind`, `--path`
and `--corpus` on the command line.

## Ask a Question

1. Open **Ask Atlas** and pick what may answer: **code**, **docs** (READMEs,
   markdown sections, synced tickets) or **all**.
2. Pick the repository, or **all repos — federated**.
3. Type the question — `how are allowed models enforced` — and press **Ask**
   or `⌘↵`.

![Typing a question into Ask Atlas and the best passage appearing below it](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-question.mp4 "Ask a question; the best passage arrives first, quoted from the file.")

The answer is the indexed text itself:

![The answer to how are allowed models enforced: summary chip, best passage from config/config.go lines 14 to 17, and the gap box](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-answer.png "The best passage: config/config.go lines 14–17, where ALLOWED_MODELS and DISALLOWED_MODELS are declared.")

- The summary chip says how many files answer and how many matches there are
  (**6 files answer · 59 matches**); the retrieval chip names the method
  (**bm25**).
- **BEST PASSAGE** quotes the lines that match, highlighted, with arrows to
  step through the other matches in the same file. **Open in Inspector**,
  **Code Map**, **Open file** and **Copy lines + citation** act on it.
- **Not in this answer** names any word of your question that matched
  nothing — here, `enforced` — so you know what the passages do not cover.
- **MORE PASSAGES** lists the other files that matched, with filters by file
  type, comments or code lines.
- **ASK NEXT** offers follow-up questions built from the matched symbols, such
  as "what calls modelDenied?". These are templates, not generated text.
- **copy link** and **export .md** share the answer; **Recent questions**
  keeps what you asked in this browser.

## Read the Exact Verdict

For questions about a symbol, the drawer at the foot of the answer — **Symbol
cards + full citation table** — holds the exact verdict. It is composed from
the index, not written by a model, and labelled as such.

![The drawer for What calls modelDenied: 5 callers of modelDenied across 1 file, key symbols and grounded evidence](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-verdict.png "What calls modelDenied? — 5 callers across 1 file, then the key symbols and 42 citations grouped by module.")

The shape of the question decides the verdict. "What calls X", "who uses X"
and "what breaks if X changes" get a callers verdict; "explain X" or "what is
X" an explain verdict; "is there…" or "do we have…" an exists verdict;
anything else a digest of the context the index served. Below the verdict come
the key symbols (each with **Inspector**, **Map**, **Ask about** and a pin),
the evidence grouped by module, and the full citation table.

## Add an AI Answer

**Synthesize with AI** adds a short answer written by a model from the
passages on the page. It is off by default and remembered per browser; the
quoted passages stay the answer either way.

1. Turn on **Synthesize with AI**.
2. Check the model picker beside it. It shows the default provider and model;
   when more than one provider is ready it is a menu.
3. Ask. The **AI SYNTHESIS** card appears above the passages.

![The Ask controls: corpus switch, repository picker, Synthesize with AI, and the model picker showing Claude claude-sonnet-5 default](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-controls.png "Synthesize with AI and the model picker, beside the corpus and repository.")

![The AI SYNTHESIS card above the best passage, with numbered citation chips and a footer naming Claude, the model, tokens and time](assets/docs/search-and-ask/ask-ai-answer.png "The AI answer, written from eight passages: each [n] opens its passage; the footer names who wrote it and what it cost.")

- Every claim must cite a passage. Each `[n]` chip scrolls to and highlights
  passage n.
- A sentence the server's check finds no valid citation for is marked
  **unsupported**; a citation to a passage that was never sent is marked as
  pointing at nothing.
- The footer states the provider, model, tokens and time — here
  `Claude (anthropic-cli) · claude-sonnet-5 · 2 in / 299 out tokens · 4667 ms`.
- If no passage matched, no model is asked.

The model reads only the question and the retrieved passages with their
paths. Which provider answers is set by `atlas llm`. With nothing configured,
Atlas detects the `claude` and `codex` CLIs and the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and
`OPENAI_API_KEY` variables, and registers what is ready. The default is the
one you chose with `atlas llm default`, else the first ready of
`anthropic-cli`, `openai-cli`, `anthropic`, `openai`. Check it with:

```sh
atlas llm status
{
  "configured": true,
  "ready": true,
  "provider": "anthropic-cli",
  "transport": "cli",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "model_source": "default",
  "rung": "cli_login",
  "rung_source": "claude login",
  …
  "egress": "the claude CLI sends the question and the retrieved passages with their paths to Anthropic under your login — nothing else leaves this machine",
  …
  "default": "anthropic-cli",
  "default_source": "detected",
  "providers": [ … ],
  …
}
```

The same providers, with a **Test** button for each, are under **System → App
integrations**. Without a ready provider the toggle shows a note pointing
there, and the passages answer alone.

For a conversation that keeps context across turns and pulls in git history,
tickets and pull requests, use the [Ask Workbench](workbench).

## Semantic Search Is Off by Default

`atlas semantic-search` ranks symbols by embedding similarity instead of
words. It needs embeddings, which the index does not build unless you ask
(`atlas index --enable-vectors` with `ATLAS_ENABLE_VECTORS=1`). Without them
it falls back to lexical search and says so:

```sh
atlas semantic-search "reject a model that is not allowed" --limit 3 --format plain
semantic_search  mode lexical  degraded true  results 3
  degraded_reason  this snapshot has no embeddings — re-index with `atlas index --enable-vectors` to enable semantic ranking
  isToolAllowed  function  internal/mcp/filter.go:32  :: func isToolAllowed(toolName, includeList, excludeList string) bool
  FilterModels  function  providers/routing/model_filter.go:35  :: func FilterModels(models []types.Model, allowedModels, disallowedModels string) []types.Model
  ALLOWED_MODELS  key  examples/docker-compose/mcp/.env.example:4  :: ALLOWED_MODELS=
```

It is off because the lexical index already answers name and phrase lookups
exactly and deterministically, with no model and nothing to download;
embeddings add indexing time and storage. By default the embedder is an
offline token-overlap model; set `ATLAS_EMBED_URL` to use a real embedding
model. See [Indexing and reindexing](indexing).

## From the CLI

Each lookup the dashboard makes is a command. Output is from
inference-gateway, in `--format plain`.

`atlas search` — the omnibox. `--kind` and `--path` filter; `--corpus docs`
searches documentation only:

```sh
atlas search "allowed models" --kind function --limit 3 --format plain
search  mode lexical  total 3
  matches  833  (page limit 3)
  truncated true  (retrieval saw fewer than the 833 matches; a larger --limit widens it, up to 20000)
  FilterModels  function  providers/routing/model_filter.go:35  :: func FilterModels(models []types.Model, allowedModels, disallowedModels string) []types.Model
  isToolAllowed  function  internal/mcp/filter.go:32  :: func isToolAllowed(toolName, includeList, excludeList string) bool
  TestChatCompletionsRouting_AllowedModelsFiltersAlias  function  tests/api_routing_test.go:206  :: func TestChatCompletionsRouting_AllowedModelsFiltersAlias(t *testing.T)

atlas search modlDenied --limit 3 --format plain
search  mode lexical  total 2
  matches  2  (page limit 3)
  modelDenied  method  api/routes.go:622  :: func (router *RouterImpl) modelDenied(model string) string
  FilterModels  function  providers/routing/model_filter.go:35  :: func FilterModels(models []types.Model, allowedModels, disallowedModels string) []types.Model
```

`atlas symbol` — a definition with its callers and callees, what the inspector
opens with:

```sh
atlas symbol modelDenied --format plain
symbol modelDenied  matches 1
  modelDenied  method  api/routes.go:622-635
    sig  func (router *RouterImpl) modelDenied(model string) string
    callers(5)  ChatCompletionsHandler, ImagesHandler, MessagesHandler, ResponsesHandler, handleImagesMultipart
    callees(6)  Error, Error, ModelMatches, ParseModelSet, Error, Error
```

`atlas snippet` — the body itself, bounded:

```sh
atlas snippet modelDenied --format plain
snippet modelDenied  definitions 1  resolved true
── api/routes.go:622-635
sig  func (router *RouterImpl) modelDenied(model string) string
func (router *RouterImpl) modelDenied(model string) string {
	if allowed := routing.ParseModelSet(router.cfg.AllowedModels); len(allowed) > 0 {
		if !routing.ModelMatches(allowed, model) {
			router.logger.Error("model not in allowed list", nil, "model", model, "allowed_models", router.cfg.AllowedModels)
			return "Model not allowed. Please check the list of allowed models."
		}
		return ""
	}
	…
}
```

`atlas explain` — a deterministic bundle: definitions, callers, callees, and
the routes served from the same file:

```sh
atlas explain modelDenied
{
  "symbol": "modelDenied",
  "definitions": [
    { "kind": "method", "path": "api/routes.go", "line": 622, "end_line": 635,
      "signature": "func (router *RouterImpl) modelDenied(model string) string" }
  ],
  "callers": ["ChatCompletionsHandler", "ImagesHandler", "MessagesHandler", "ResponsesHandler", "handleImagesMultipart"],
  "callees": ["Error", "ModelMatches", "ParseModelSet"],

    { "method": "GET", "path": "/health", "handler_file": "api/routes.go" },
    { "method": "POST", "path": "/chat/completions", "handler_file": "api/routes.go" },
    …
  ],
  …
}
```

`atlas callers` lists the symbols that call a function; `atlas refs` adds
type uses — parameters, fields, return types — which matters before a rename:

```sh
atlas callers modelDenied --format plain

atlas refs CreateChatCompletionRequest --format plain
refs CreateChatCompletionRequest  total 44
  Middleware  method  api/middlewares/mcp.go:86  :: func (m *MCPMiddlewareImpl) Middleware() gin.HandlerFunc
  handleMCPStreamingRequest  method  api/middlewares/mcp.go:242  :: func (m *MCPMiddlewareImpl) handleMCPStreamingRequest(c *gin.Context, request *types.CreateChatCompletionRequest, result *MCPProviderModelResult) error
  …
```

All flags are in the [CLI reference](cli).

## How Fresh Is the Answer

**Since 0.1.55**, every answer about a repository says which snapshot it came
from and whether the code has moved since: `indexed_sha`, `head_sha`, `dirty`,
`stale` and `stale_reason`, the same on the CLI, over MCP and from the API
([#59](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/59)). Edit a file after
indexing and the next lookup says so before anything else:

```text
$ atlas snippet helper --format plain
stale: indexed 4fb9d0f74f1c vs head 4fb9d0f74f1c+dirty  (working_tree_dirty)  not refreshed (one-shot command; run `atlas index`)
snippet helper  definitions 1  resolved true
```

`resolved: true` still means the symbol was found; `stale: true` means its
line numbers and body may have moved. A one-shot command does not refresh in
the background, so run `atlas index .`, or set `ATLAS_ONESHOT_REFRESH=sync`
to refresh before answering
([#141](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/141)). Indexing uncommitted
work stores its own `<sha>+dirty` snapshot beside the commit's — see
[Change lens and history](history).

## Answers That Refuse Instead of Guessing

Keyword search always matches something, so a list of citations is not proof
that the code answers the question. When an assistant or a script calls
`code_query` with `require_citations: true`, **since 0.1.55** the cited names
and paths must carry what the question names — an identifier it spells, or
enough of its specific words ([#60](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/60)).
Otherwise the answer is `status: "insufficient"` with
`reason: "citations_below_relevance_floor"`, a `relevance` block naming the
words nothing matched, and the nearest candidates as `low_confidence_hits`,
never as citations. Asked about "the quantum flux capacitor module" in a
repository that has none, Atlas now says so instead of citing a `helper`
whose doc comment mentions "module". The fields are described in
[MCP tools](mcp).

## Evidence Inside Large Functions

The index keeps the start and end of a long function body, not every line.
**Since 0.1.55**, when a question is about something inside a long function —
a route registered on line 1,005 of a 2,000-line setup function — `code_query`
and `context` re-read the matching lines from the file, as long as the file
still matches the index, and quote them with every skipped run marked
`// ... elided N lines (La-Lb) ...`. The answer's `metadata.body_elision`
lists the line ranges shown, and the citation keeps the function's real range
([#156](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/156)).

## From the API

The page names its own sources: `GET /api/v1/search` for the omnibox and
related symbols, `GET /api/v1/passages` for the quoted passages,
`POST /api/v1/agent/code-query` for the verdict drawer, and
`POST /api/v1/ask/answer` for the AI answer, which streams and takes a
`provider` per question. See [Dashboard and API](service).

- [Ask Workbench](workbench) — conversations with history, tickets and pull
  requests.

  inspector.
