# Ask Workbench
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/workbench/

# Ask Workbench

The Ask Workbench is a conversation about your codebase, held inside the Atlas
dashboard. You ask in plain language; Atlas gathers the evidence — code
passages from its index, git history, and the tickets, pull requests and
findings of the sources you connected — plus what it computed itself (routes
tables, usage counts, definitions, last changes); a model you choose writes the
answer, citing that evidence line by line. Every citation opens the record it
came from, and every thread is kept by the server so you can come back to it.

The Workbench needs a running service ([Dashboard and HTTP API](service)) and
an AI provider ([AI assistant setup](assistants)). Without a provider it still
answers, with Atlas's own deterministic verdict and facts.

## Open It

```sh
atlas serve
```

Open the dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:3099/dashboard`) and choose **Ask
Workbench**. The composer takes a question; the chips beneath it pick the
repository, the sources to consult (Git, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, Pulse — the
ones your service has connected), and the model.

A first question starts a thread. Every later question in the same composer
continues it: the server keeps the turns, and the model reads the earlier ones
as context. The rail on the left lists your threads; `#/workbench?thread=<id>`
reopens one without re-asking anything.

![Typing a question into the Ask Workbench composer, sending it, and the answer streaming in as a routes table](assets/docs/workbench/ask-a-question.mp4 "Asking on inference-gateway: the Atlas and Git lanes answer first (11 and 3 items), then Claude (claude-sonnet-5) writes. This turn took 7.2 s from plan to done.")

## What Happens in a Turn

1. **Plan.** Atlas reads the question, resolves its scope (a repository, a
   file, a symbol, a ticket or a pull request) and plans which sources to ask.
2. **Gather.** The sources run in parallel: the index returns the passages and
   definitions that match, git blames the lines the question points at,
   GitHub, Jira, Confluence and Pulse return their records. When the question
   asks who changed something or which of two things is actually used, Atlas
   pre-fetches the blame and the callers so the model has them from the start.
3. **Compute.** Atlas builds its exact verdict and facts — the routes table, the
   usage summary, the definitions, the last change — and hands them to the
   model as labelled evidence (`S1`…`S5`) beside the passages (`A…`), commits
   (`G…`), tickets (`J…`), pages (`C…`) and findings (`P…`).
4. **Answer.** The model writes the answer in whatever shape the question
   calls for — a sentence, a list, a table, a walk-through — citing the labels
   inline. A multi-part question is answered part by part.
5. **Ask for more.** When the evidence does not cover something Atlas could
   fetch, the model asks for it (a symbol's whole body, a file, a search, the
   callers of a function, a git blame, a ticket) and Atlas resolves the request
   in well under a second. If the model answered first and then asked, it
   revises the answer once as a patch: only the sections the new evidence
   changes are rewritten, and they are marked. By default a turn makes at most
   three model calls and one revision; what the model would still like to
   fetch is offered as a follow-up suggestion instead.

The whole turn streams, so you watch the sources answer, the model write, and
the revision land.

![The Run tab of the side panel: Planned, Atlas gathered 17 items, Exact verdict, Claude answered, Checked, Done](assets/docs/workbench/side-run.png "The Run tab tells the same turn back: planned at 48 ms, 17 items gathered, the exact verdict at 288 ms, Claude answered in 6.4 s, all 5 statements checked, done at 7.2 s.")

## Reading an Answer

![A finished Workbench answer: a table of 10 routes with method, path and handler, each handler cited with a chip from A1 to A10](assets/docs/workbench/finished-answer.png "A finished answer. The table lists the 10 routes main.main registers; each handler carries its citation chip (A1–A10) and the count cites the computed routes table (S1).")

- **Citations** are chips (`A3`, `G1`, `J2`). Click one for the evidence: the
  passage with its path and lines, the commit, the ticket. Ticket keys, pull
  request numbers and commit hashes in the prose are links to Jira or GitHub
  when the turn holds that record; file paths and symbols link to the Code Map.
- **How Atlas got here** (below the answer) opens the deterministic trail: the
  exact facts with their source tags, the plan, the routes table, every
  evidence item.
- **The trust cue** in the footer counts the statements that cite evidence and
  flags the ones that do not; **Check** opens the graded view.
- **Copy**, **Link** and **Re-ask** sit in the footer. Copy gives the answer as
  Markdown with its sources; Link is a permalink to the turn at its snapshot;
  Re-ask runs the same question again at that snapshot as a new turn.
- **Follow up** chips under the last turn are the model's suggested next
  questions; the composer continues the thread.

![The popover of citation A5: POST /chat/completions, handler ChatCompletionsHandler, registered at cmd/gateway/main.go:316, with Open in Code Map, Inspector, Pin and Copy](assets/docs/workbench/citation-popover.png "Clicking A5 opens its evidence: POST /chat/completions, served by ChatCompletionsHandler (api/routes.go) and registered at cmd/gateway/main.go:316, at snapshot 5249675.")

![How Atlas got here, expanded below the answer: What Atlas found, a list of facts tagged real, then the routes table grouped by router](assets/docs/workbench/how-atlas-got-here.png "How Atlas got here, opened: the scope, intent and snapshot, the facts Atlas found (each tagged real and cited), then the routes table grouped by router.")

![The end of a turn: source lanes, the model chip, 7.2 s, How Atlas got here, All 5 statements cite evidence, Copy, Link, Re-ask, and three Follow up suggestions](assets/docs/workbench/follow-up.png "The end of the turn: the source lanes, the model chip and time, How Atlas got here, the trust cue (All 5 statements cite evidence), Copy · Link · Re-ask, and the Follow up suggestions.")

## The Side Panel

The panel on the right follows the selected turn and names it ("Turn 2 of 3 ·
10:24 · 3 rounds · revised once · 48 s"), with ‹ › to move between turns.

- **Evidence** lists everything the turn gathered, by source.
- **Inspector** shows one item in full; pin a chip to keep it there.
- **Run** tells the turn as a timeline — planned, gathered, answered, asked,
  fetched, revised, checked, done — with the time each step took. The
  **Conversation** scope shows where the time went across every turn.
- **Tokens** shows what the turn cost: the prompt the model read (input,
  including the prompt cache), its output, the time, and the budget; per model
  call inside the turn, and totals across the conversation with one row per
  question.

![The Evidence tab: the CODE lane with A1 to A10 routes, A11 main.main, S1 Routes table and S4 Last change](assets/docs/workbench/side-evidence.png "Evidence, by lane: ten routes (A1–A10), the registrar main.main (A11) and the facts Atlas computed (S1, S4…).")

![The Tokens tab: about 2,394 tokens of evidence, 6,482 model input and 547 output tokens, the model, and the hourly budget](assets/docs/workbench/side-tokens.png "Tokens for the same turn: about 2,394 tokens of evidence, 6,482 input and 547 output tokens as the provider reported them, and 1 of 30 model turns used this hour.")

## Threads, Ownership and Sharing

Threads live in the service's database, not in the browser. On a laptop's own
Atlas every thread belongs to you. A shared service (one that identifies its
callers through a Jira OAuth session or a gateway identity header) keeps each
thread private to its owner unless the owner shares it with the tenant; an
operator token sees all of them, a read-only token sees shared ones. Rename,
share and delete from the thread's header.

![The thread rail open over the answer: Threads, + New, and one thread from today with its turn count and verdict](assets/docs/workbench/thread-rail.png "☰ Threads opens the rail: each thread with its age, turn count and verdict. ✎ renames, × deletes, + New starts another thread.")

## Use It from the API

The Workbench is an HTTP route like every other dashboard feature, so a script
or another tool can ask the same questions:

```sh
# ask, streaming the turn as server-sent events (thread_id continues a thread)
curl -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3099/api/v1/ask/workbench \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"what are the auth routes, and who last changed the login one?"}'

# the threads the server keeps
curl http://127.0.0.1:3099/api/v1/ask/workbench/threads
curl http://127.0.0.1:3099/api/v1/ask/workbench/threads/<id>
```

The stream's frames — `thread`, `plan`, `agent.*`, `merge`, `verify`, `meta`,
`delta`, `more`, `usage`, `patch`, `done` — are described in `openapi.json` on
the running service. A thread is read with `GET …/threads/{id}`, renamed with
`PATCH`, deleted with `DELETE`; `DELETE …/threads` removes all of the caller's
threads. Reads need the read-only token or better where a token is set; writes
need the read-write token.

## Choosing the Model

The Workbench uses the same providers as the Ask page's AI answers: a `claude`
or `codex` CLI that is installed and logged in is detected automatically, and
an API key can be stored with `atlas llm set`. `atlas llm status` shows what is
configured and which models the provider offers; the composer's model menu
lists those models. On the Claude CLI, a call that only decides what Atlas
should fetch runs at low reasoning effort; the answer runs at the CLI's default
unless `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_ANSWER_EFFORT` says otherwise.

## What Leaves the Machine

Only when a model is configured and a question is asked: the question, the
labelled evidence the turn gathered (passages, never whole files; records from
the connected sources), the earlier turns of the thread as context, and the
instructions. Nothing is sent when no provider is configured, and nothing is
sent for the exact verdict. See [Privacy and Data Handling](privacy).

## Limits and Settings

| Setting | Default | What it bounds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_MODEL_ROUNDS` | `3` | Model calls one answer may make (an answer, plus rounds of asking Atlas for more) |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_MODEL_REVISIONS` | `1` | Times an answer may be written again after the model asked for more |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_MAX_EVIDENCE_TOKENS` | `24000` | Evidence a prompt may carry; past it the prompt is trimmed and the trimmed items are listed |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_ANSWER_MAX_TOKENS` | `4000` | The longest reply, on the API providers |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_ASK_EFFORT` / `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_ANSWER_EFFORT` | `low` / the CLI's own | Reasoning effort of an asking call and of an answering call on the Claude CLI |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_HISTORY_TURNS` / `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_HISTORY_RUNES` | `6` / `4000` | How much of the thread the model reads as context |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_MODEL_TURNS_PER_HOUR` | `30` | Model turns per token per hour; past it a turn answers with the exact verdict only |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_TURNS_PER_HOUR` | `240` | Turns per token per hour; past it the route answers `429` with `retry_after` |
| `ATLAS_WORKBENCH_MODEL_FORMAT` | `answer` | `chat` switches back to the earlier two-part explanation format |

`atlas config list` prints every setting with its current value; see
[Configuration](configuration) for precedence.

## When It Does Not Answer

- **"Exact only" and no model chip**: no provider is configured or detected.
  `atlas llm status` says why; `atlas llm detect --apply` registers a logged-in
  CLI.
- **`llm_auth_failed` although the CLI is logged in**: the service could not
  probe the CLI in time — typically a VPN or endpoint-security agent slowing
  every process launch on the host. Ask again without the tunnel, or store an
  API key so no subprocess is needed.
- **"The model is off for this question"**: the hourly model budget for your
  token is spent; the exact verdict still answers.
- **A thread answers 404**: it is not yours to see on a shared service, or it
  was deleted.

See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting) for service-level problems.

---

# Impact and Review
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/impact/

# Impact and review

Impact answers the question you ask before you change something: what else
does this reach? You name the symbols or files you are about to change; Atlas
walks the stored call and import edges backwards to every symbol, file and test
that could notice, and joins the result with the routes the repository serves
and the repositories that call them. Reach for it before a refactor, while
reviewing a pull request, or when you need to know which tests to run.

## Open It

In the dashboard, choose **Impact** in the EXPLORE group (`#/impact`). The view
opens on the first repository with nothing picked. Everything you pick is
written into the address — `#/impact?repo=<repo>&symbols=a,b&depth=3` — so a
radius can be linked and reopened.

![The Impact view before anything is picked: Repository, Add a symbol to the change set, depth and Compute radius](assets/docs/impact/impact-empty.png "Impact with nothing picked yet. The radius appears under the picker.")

From a terminal, the same question is one command. Positional arguments are
symbols; changed files go in `--paths`:

```sh
atlas impact StreamChatCompletions
atlas impact --paths api/context_window.go
```

## Find What a Change Reaches

![Typing StreamChatCompletions into the Impact picker, choosing the provider method, and the blast radius appearing](assets/docs/impact/pick-a-symbol.mp4 "Picking StreamChatCompletions on inference-gateway. The radius computes as soon as a symbol is picked.")

1. Choose the **Repository**.
2. Type a name into **Add a symbol to the change set…**. The list offers only
   symbols the index holds, with their kind and `path:line`; free text is never
   accepted as a symbol.
3. Pick one. The radius computes at once. Add more symbols (up to 12) to widen
   the change set; **×** on a chip removes it.
4. **depth** (1 to 6, default 3) bounds how many reverse hops the walk takes.
   **Compute radius** runs it again.

**One name, every definition.** A name stands for every definition that
carries it. In inference-gateway, `StreamChatCompletions` is an interface
method, the provider's method and two test mocks, so the verdict starts from 4
seeds and lists all four under **traversal roots**.

## Read the Radius

![The Impact verdict: Changing these 4 seeds would touch 10 symbols across 8 files, the traversal roots, the impacted symbols and the impacted files grouped by module](assets/docs/impact/impact-radius.png "The radius of StreamChatCompletions: 10 symbols across 8 files at depth 3, with 6 covering tests.")

- **The verdict** — "Changing these 4 seeds would touch 10 symbols across 8
  files", with the depth reached and the number of covering tests. It is
  labelled **structural verdict**: counted from stored edges, not written by a
  model. **Copy link to this radius** copies the address.
- **Impacted symbols** are chips; each opens the Symbol Inspector.
- **Impacted files** are grouped by module (here `tests` 4, `api` 2,
  `internal/mcp` 2), each with the reason the server gave — `caller` for all
  eight.
- **Covering tests in the radius** lists the tests that reach the change, with
  `path:line`: the list to run before you merge.
- **Affected routes** are the contracts whose handler symbol and file are both
  in the radius — here `POST /chat/completions` through
  `ChatCompletionsHandler`. Contracts that only share a file are counted, not
  listed.
- **Cross-repo blast** checks whether another indexed repository calls a route
  served from the impacted files. On this single-repository demo it reads "no
  call site in another repo hits a route served from these files (10 served
  routes in the closure, 42 changed paths checked)".

![Further down the radius: impacted files by module, covering tests with path and line, the affected route POST /chat/completions, and the cross-repo line](assets/docs/impact/impact-tests-routes.png "Covering tests, the affected route and the cross-repo line for the same radius.")

An empty radius is a finding, not an error: no stored edge reaches the seeds.

## Read the Routes a Repository Serves

Choose **Routes** in the EXPLORE group (`#/routes`). It lists the HTTP
contracts the index proved, each with its method, path pattern, handler, file
and the server's **CONF** (confidence) verbatim. The filter box narrows by
path, handler or method; **all** / **≥ medium** / **high only** sets a
confidence floor. Rows are grouped by the module of the handler's file.

![The Routes view for inference-gateway: 20 contracts, 7 GET, 11 POST, 1 ALL, 1 ANY, 10 medium and 10 low confidence, with the api group of 9 routes](assets/docs/impact/routes-table.png "inference-gateway serves 20 contracts: 7 GET, 11 POST, 1 ALL and 1 ANY; 10 medium and 10 low confidence.")

Of the 20, eleven are registered by `cmd/gateway/main.go` (one of them,
`POST /metrics`, is handled by a test mock) and nine by the example MCP servers
under `examples/`. `atlas stats` reports 71 route rows for the snapshot: 32 are
outbound HTTP calls the gateway makes, and the rest are the registrations this
view folds into 20 contracts.

On a row:

- The **handler** name opens the Symbol Inspector.
- **chain** opens the Inspector with the handler's callers, references and
  neighbours loaded.
- The crosshair button opens **Impact** for that handler.
- A click anywhere else opens the **Dependency panel** under the row:
  **IMPLEMENTS — SAME REPO** (the handler's call chain from the stored graph)
  and **CONSUMED BY — OTHER REPOS** (call sites in other indexed repositories
  that match this route).

![The Dependency panel under POST /chat/completions: IMPLEMENTS shows ChatCompletionsHandler at api/routes.go:46, CONSUMED BY shows no recorded call site in another repo](assets/docs/impact/routes-dependency.png "The Dependency panel of POST /chat/completions. The graph records no outgoing call edge from the handler; no other repository calls the route.")

## Find Who Calls a Route from Another Repository

Cross-repo answers join two repositories: the routes one serves and the HTTP
calls another makes. Three commands ask it from either side:

- `atlas consumers` — the other repositories that call a route this one serves.
- `atlas dependencies` — the producers and handlers that serve the calls this
  one makes.
- `atlas cross-repo-impact --paths <files>` — which other repositories call the
  routes served by the handlers in the changed files.

The demo service holds one code repository, so every join is empty. This is
the real output, and the shape a populated answer fills:

```sh
atlas consumers --format plain
```

```text
consumers inference-gateway  impacted 0/0  repos 0/0
  producer  52496750  indexed 2026-10-28T05:16:55Z
```

```sh
atlas cross-repo-impact --paths api/routes.go
```

```json
{
  "repo": "inference-gateway",
  "served_routes": [
    { "method": "GET", "path_pattern": "/health",
      "handler_file": "api/routes.go", "handler_symbol": "HealthcheckHandler",
      "confidence": "medium", "registered_in": "cmd/gateway/main.go", "registered_line": 310 },
    …
  ],
  "impacted": [],
  "consumer_repos": [],
  "producer_commit": "524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
  "closure_size": 13,
  "effective_changed_paths": 14,
  "total_served_routes": 10
}
```

With a second repository indexed — a front end or another service whose code
calls these paths — `impacted` lists each matched route with the calling file
and symbol, and `consumer_repos` names the callers. The same joins feed the
**CONSUMED BY** half of the Dependency panel, the cross-repo line of Impact,
and the **Repos** lens of the Code Map, which draws a repo-pair matrix: rows
consume, columns produce.

![The Code Map Repos lens: a repo-pair matrix of github://github, inference-gateway and prometheus://promlabs, all zero, and the note No cross-repo route join recorded](assets/docs/impact/repos-lens.png "The Repos lens on the demo. The other two rows are connected sources, which serve no routes, so every cell is 0.")

## Gather Review Context for a Change

Three read-only commands prepare a review. `atlas context` builds a bounded
bundle around changed paths — the changed symbols with excerpts, retrieval hits
for an optional question, the impacted files and the edges between them — sized
for a model's context window:

```sh
atlas context --format plain --paths providers/core/provider.go "how are streaming chat completions forwarded"
```

```text
context  mode symbol_context  files 13  symbols 32  edges 17  hits 4  impacted 0
  files(13)  providers/core/provider.go, internal/guardrails/guardrails.go, logger/logger.go, …
  symbols(29)  HTTPError, StatusCode, Message, Error, ProviderImpl, ID, Name, URL, Token, …
```

`atlas receipt` compares a git base with `HEAD` against the local snapshot and
prints what the diff touches. It never indexes or writes anything:

```sh
atlas receipt --base HEAD~3
```

```text
Atlas pre-submit receipt
changed paths: 4
changed symbols:
  VERSION — callers ambiguous (config/meta.go:5)
  TracesEndpointURL — callers 2 (otel/otel.go:86)
  Init — callers ambiguous (otel/otel.go:104)
  TestTracingTracesEndpointURL — callers 0 (tests/tracing_test.go:312)
caller note: ambiguous means multiple same-named definitions; count withheld
served routes touched: 10
consumer repos: 0
local snapshot e842033e · commit 52496750 · NOT the server's snapshot
```

`atlas coverage` lists the tests that reach a symbol. Without an imported
coverage profile it answers from the call graph (`mode static`);
`atlas coverage import` loads a Go coverprofile or LCOV file for real line
coverage:

```sh
atlas coverage --format plain StreamChatCompletions
```

```text
coverage StreamChatCompletions  mode static  covered true  dir tests_for_symbol
  tests(20)  TestRunWithStreamReturnsWhenConsumerAbandons, TestChatCompletionsHandler_StreamingErrorHandling, TestChatCompletionsRouting_StreamingPassthrough, TestAgent_RunWithStream, …
```

## From the CLI

```sh
atlas impact StreamChatCompletions --format plain
```

```text
impact  symbols 10  files 8  tests 6  depth 3
  symbols(10)  ChatCompletionsHandler, Middleware, RunWithStream, TestAgent_RunWithStream, …
  files(8)  api/middlewares/mcp.go, api/routes.go, internal/mcp/agent.go, internal/mcp/client_concurrency_test.go, …
  tests(6)  TestRunWithStreamReturnsWhenConsumerAbandons, TestChatCompletionsHandler_StreamingErrorHandling, …
```

```sh
atlas route-contracts --format plain
```

```text
route_contracts inference-gateway  total 20
  ALL /mcp  confidence low  source route_table
  ANY /metrics  Handler  confidence low  source route_table
  GET /  confidence low  source route_table
  GET /capabilities  func  confidence low  source route_table
  GET /health  HealthcheckHandler  confidence medium  source route_table
  …
```

`--max-depth` bounds the walk (default 3) and `--tests=false` leaves out
covering tests. The [CLI reference](cli) lists every flag.

## From the API and MCP

The views read these routes on the running service ([Dashboard and API](service)):

| Route | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/impact` | The radius: `{"symbols": […], "repo_id": "…", "max_depth": 3}` |
| `GET /api/v1/repos/{repo}/route-contracts` | The routes a repository serves, paged with `next_offset` |
| `GET /api/v1/repos/{repo}/consumers` · `/dependencies` | Cross-repo callers and producers |
| `GET /api/v1/repos/{repo}/consumer-contracts` | Every outbound call the repository makes, matched or not |
| `POST /api/v1/repos/{repo}/cross-repo-impact` | Cross-repo blast for `{"changed_paths": […]}` |

An assistant asks the same questions over MCP through the `impact` tool (with
`scope=cross_repo` for the cross-repo radius), `routes` and `context`. See
[MCP tools](mcp).

## Related

- [Code Map and graph](code-map) — walk the callers and callees a radius is made of.
- [Change lens and history](history) — what an indexing pass changed, and how history grows.
- [Ask Workbench](workbench) — ask about a change in plain language, with citations.
- [MCP tools](mcp) — the same answers for an AI assistant.

# Change Lens and History
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/history/

# Change lens and history

Every indexing pass stores a snapshot: the files, symbols, call edges and routes
of a repository at one commit. History is what you read from those snapshots —
what a pass added, changed and removed, which symbols carry the most weight, and
whether the index still matches the code. With logs connected, the same idea
applies to a running service: what it started or stopped saying between two
windows. Reach for it after a merge, before a release, or when an answer and the
code seem to disagree.

## Open It

The views live in three places in the dashboard's navigation:

- **Changes** in EXPLORE (`#/changes`) — the Change Lens: the snapshot timeline
  and what each pass changed.
- **Hot Symbols** (`#/hot`) and **Freshness** (`#/staleness`) in CODEBASE — the
  graph's hubs and the freshness of what Atlas derives from the latest snapshot.
- **What Changed** in OBSERVE (`#/diff`) — two windows of one log stream
  compared. OBSERVE appears once Loki or Elasticsearch is configured.

![The Change Lens: a repository picker, the snapshot timeline with one snapshot 5249675, and the notice One snapshot recorded — a diff needs two](assets/docs/history/change-lens-one-snapshot.png "The Change Lens on the demo service, which holds one snapshot of inference-gateway.")

From a terminal, `atlas history` prints the same timeline:

```sh
atlas history --format plain
```

```text
history inference-gateway  snapshots 1
  52496750  e842033e-41d6-4e7a-9e27-7415bc5edcbc  files 307  symbols 11092  edges 13900  2026-10-28T05:16:55Z
```

## See What an Indexing Pass Changed

1. Open **Changes** and choose the **Repository**.
2. The **Snapshot timeline** lists every stored snapshot, newest first: the
   short commit, its symbol, edge and file counts, and its age.
3. Pick a snapshot. The lens compares it with the snapshot indexed just before
   it and answers "what did this pass change?": a count verdict first, then
   **Added symbols**, **Modified symbols**, **Removed symbols**, the changed
   files, and **Added call edges** and **Removed call edges**.

Added and modified symbols open the Symbol Inspector; removed ones do not,
because they no longer exist in the newer snapshot. Changed files open in
Files. The server sends at most 100 rows per list, while the counts are always
complete, so a long list says "first 100 of N". The address keeps the pick
(`#/changes?repo=<repo>&to=<snapshot>`).

![The snapshot timeline with one entry, 5249675 with 11,092 symbols, 13,900 edges and 307 files, beside the instruction to index again and the command atlas index path](assets/docs/history/change-lens-timeline.png "With one snapshot there is nothing to compare, and the lens says how to get a second one.")

The demo store holds a single snapshot (commit `5249675`, 11,092 symbols), so
the lens shows its empty state. History grows by indexing again once the code
has moved — after a pull, a merge or a checkout of another commit:

```sh
git pull
atlas index .
```

Each pass at a new commit stores another snapshot, and the lens then diffs it
against the one before. Retention keeps the newest 5 snapshots per repository
by default (`ATLAS_MAX_SNAPSHOTS_PER_REPO`); the current one is never deleted.
See [Indexing and reindexing](indexing).

## Compare Two Snapshots from the CLI

`atlas snapshot-diff` (alias `atlas diff`) gives the same structural delta in a
terminal: symbols and edges added, removed and modified. `--to` defaults to the
latest snapshot and `--from` to the one before it; both take a commit sha (a
prefix is enough) or a snapshot id.

```sh
atlas snapshot-diff --format plain
```

```text
atlas: need two snapshots to diff — index the repo at two commits, or pass --from
```

That is the real answer on a store with one snapshot. `--from` names the base
explicitly; pointed at the one stored snapshot it compares the snapshot with
itself, which shows the shape of an answer with every count at zero:

```sh
atlas snapshot-diff --from 5249675
```

```json
{
  "from_commit": "524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
  "to_commit": "524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
  "added_count": 0,
  "removed_count": 0,
  "modified_count": 0,
  "added_symbols": [],
  "removed_symbols": [],
  "modified_symbols": [],
  "changed_files": [],
  "added_edges": [],
  "removed_edges": []
}
```

`atlas snapshots list` shows what history is costing on disk — one row per
stored snapshot with its counts, and the retention policy:

```sh
atlas snapshots list
```

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    {
      "repo_full_name": "inference-gateway",
      "snapshot_count": 1,
      "snapshots": [
        { "commit_sha": "524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
          "created_at": "2026-10-28T05:16:55Z",
          "file_count": 307, "symbol_count": 11092, "edge_count": 13900,
          "route_count": 71, "current": true }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "retention": { "max_snapshots_per_repo": 5, "max_total_bytes": 5368709120, "max_age": "disabled" }
}
```

`atlas snapshots prune --dry-run` prints exactly what a prune would delete
without touching anything; `--keep N` and `--keep-since 90d` override the
policy for one run.

## Snapshots of Uncommitted Work

**Since 0.1.55**, indexing a working tree with uncommitted edits or untracked
files stores a snapshot of its own, labelled `<sha>+dirty`, beside the clean
snapshot of that commit ([#65](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/65)).
The timeline lists both, and `snapshot-diff` compares them: `--from` and `--to`
accept `<sha>+dirty` as well as a commit sha or a snapshot id. On a small
repository after adding one function without committing it:

```text
$ atlas history --format plain
history repo  snapshots 2
  4fb9d0f7+dirty  e0596478-…  files 2  symbols 4  edges 3  2026-10-29T05:18:49Z
  4fb9d0f7  777a3e52-…  files 2  symbols 3  edges 3  2026-10-29T05:18:35Z

$ atlas snapshot-diff --format plain
snapshot_diff 4fb9d0f7 -> 4fb9d0f7+dirty  +1 -0 ~0  files 1
  added(1)  extra
  files(1)  main.go
```

In `snapshots list` the dirty row carries `dirty: true` and its `tree_hash`.
A newer dirty state of the same commit retires the one before it, so edit
churn never pushes commit history out of the per-repository cap, and
committing the work stores the new commit's snapshot.

## Find the Symbols That Carry the Most Weight

**Hot Symbols** ranks the graph's hubs by total degree — the calls in plus the
calls out. A hub is where a change spreads: a symbol many others call, or one
that calls many others.

![Hot Symbols: the hub leaderboard with main at degree 71, ProviderImpl.ListModels and RouterImpl.handleImagesMultipart at 55, and the detail rail for main](assets/docs/history/hot-symbols.png "The hub leaderboard of inference-gateway. main in cmd/gateway/main.go leads with 71 outgoing edges and none incoming.")

- **DEGREE**, **IN** and **OUT** are counted from stored edges; **RANK** orders
  the board. Click a column head to sort.
- The filter box narrows by symbol name or repository; the chips filter by the
  **SOURCE** column (every hub on the demo reads **yes**: backed by the current
  graph).
- The rail on the right describes the selected hub — its graph signal ("Low
  inbound degree" for `main`), kind, degree and rank — with **Inspect symbol**
  and **View in Code Map**.

```sh
atlas hubs --format plain
```

```text
hubs  total 20
  main  function  in 0  out 71  total 71  cmd/gateway/main.go
  ProviderImpl.ListModels  method  in 2  out 53  total 55  providers/core/provider.go
  RouterImpl.handleImagesMultipart  method  in 2  out 53  total 55  api/routes.go
  RouterImpl.MessagesHandler  method  in 0  out 52  total 52  api/routes.go
  LoggerZapImpl.Error  method  in 41  out 6  total 47  logger/logger.go
  …
```

Since 0.1.55 a hub needs at least one resolved call or inheritance relation:
the header adds `eligible` and `excluded_isolated`, and on a sparse graph the
list is shorter than the limit rather than padded with symbols nothing calls
([#45](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/45)).

## Check How Fresh the Index Is

**Freshness** lists the operations Atlas derives from the latest snapshot — on
the demo, one **Observe repo** card per indexed repository — and checks each
against two signals: **Code** (the snapshot it was built from is still the one
loaded) and **Time** (when that snapshot was indexed). Hover a signal for its
detail. A card whose signals all hold reads **fresh**; the badge at the top
counts the stale ones. **Inspect** opens the operation.

![The Freshness view: three cards, Observe repo github://github, inference-gateway and prometheus://promlabs, each fresh with 2/2 signals, and the badge 0 stale](assets/docs/history/freshness.png "Three operations, each fresh on both signals; 0 stale.")

When the code moves on and the index does not, re-index: `atlas index .` brings
the snapshot, and with it every derived operation, up to date.
[Indexing and reindexing](indexing) covers watching a repository so this
happens on every change.

The answers themselves say how fresh they are too. Since 0.1.55 every
lookup carries `indexed_sha`, `head_sha`, `dirty` and `stale`, and a plain
answer opens with a `stale:` line when the checkout has moved past the
snapshot that answered — see [Search and Ask](search-and-ask)
([#59](https://github.com/aziron-ai/atlas/issues/59)).

## See What a Service Started or Stopped Saying

**What Changed** compares two windows of one log stream from its hourly counts:
templates **New in B**, **Gone in B**, and **Rate changed** per minute, biggest
move first. Each row names the line of code that emits the template in
**CALLER**. Choose the stream, then one shape: **Recent window** (the last
1–24 h against the same length before), **Around an instant** (either side of a
deploy) or **Explicit windows**, and press **Compare**.

![What Changed for prod / inference-gateway: Gone in B has route not found, Rate changed shows failed to generate tokens up 187 percent, with callers such as api/routes.go:805](assets/docs/history/what-changed.png "The last hour of the prod stream against the hour before. failed to generate tokens (api/routes.go:805) is up 187 % per minute; route not found stopped.")

Windows widen to whole UTC hours and are echoed back; a window still running is
marked partial and its rates use the minutes elapsed, and a window that starts
before the stream was first ingested is flagged as undercounted. The same
comparison from a terminal:

```sh
atlas logs diff --stream inference-gateway --scope prod --window 1h --format plain
```

```text
stream inference-gateway  scope prod  limit 20  new 0 of 0  gone 1 of 1  changed 6 of 6
WINDOW  FROM                  TO                    MINUTES                 TEMPLATES  LINES
a       2026-10-28T04:00:00Z  2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  60                      7          120
b       2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  2026-10-28T07:00:00Z  75.88 of 120 (partial)  6          177

LIST     COUNT_A  COUNT_B  CHANGE  SEVERITY  CALLER                    SKELETON
gone     5        0        -100%   warn      api/routes.go:98          route not found
changed  12       44       +190%   error     api/routes.go:805         failed to generate tokens | err <*>:{<*>:<*>,<*>:<*>
…
```

Connecting a log source and the other Observe views are covered in
[Observe](observe).

## From the API

| Route | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/history?repo=<repo>` | The snapshot timeline |
| `GET /api/v1/snapshot-diff?repo=<repo>&from=<sha>` | The structural delta; `422` with the "need two snapshots" detail when there is only one |
| `GET /api/v1/logs/diff` | The two-window comparison What Changed draws |

An assistant reads the timeline over MCP with the `history` tool
([MCP tools](mcp)). Every command and flag is in the [CLI reference](cli); the
service is described in [Dashboard and API](service).

## Related

- [Indexing and reindexing](indexing) — how snapshots are made and kept current.
- [Impact and review](impact) — what a change you are about to make will reach.
- [Code Map and graph](code-map) — open a hub and walk its neighbourhood.
- [Observe](observe) — log streams, incidents, alerts, builds and traces.

# Connected Sources
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/sources/

# Connected sources

A connected source brings the records around your code — pull requests and
issues, tickets, wiki pages, dashboards and alert rules, builds, traces, drive
files — into Atlas as a virtual repository. Each record becomes a real file with
real line ranges, indexed like code, so a citation into a pull request validates
by path and hash exactly the way a citation into a function does. Reach for it
when the answer you need is the why behind the code: the ticket that asked for
a change, the pull request that made it, the alert that fires on it.

## Open It

Sources are added and synced from the CLI. Two dashboard pages show them:

- **Connectors** in FLEET (`#/connectors`) — the monitoring kinds (Prometheus,
  Grafana, Jenkins, Tempo) beside the log pulls, each with its status and a
  **Configure** form.
- **System** → **App integrations** (`#/system?tab=integrations`) — the GitHub
  and Pulse lanes of the Ask Workbench, and Jira sign-in.

![The Connectors view: cards for Grafana Loki, Elasticsearch, Prometheus, Grafana, Jenkins, Jenkins console pull and Tempo, two of them configured](assets/docs/sources/connectors-view.png "Connectors on the demo service: a Loki log pull and the public Prometheus at demo.promlabs.com are configured; the other cards wait for Configure.")

In a terminal, `atlas source list` shows what is configured and
`atlas source status` what each source has actually synced.

## Choose a Kind

Eight kinds are registered. Each turns its records into Markdown documents
under its own virtual repository (`github://<name>`, `prometheus://<name>`, …):

| Kind | What becomes a document | Credential | Also feeds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `github` | Pull requests and issues of each `--repo owner/name`, as `github/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>.md` and `…/issue/<n>.md` | `--token-env GITHUB_TOKEN` | The Workbench's GitHub lane |
| `jira` | The issues of `--project KEY` (or a `--jql` filter) | `--email` and `--token-env`; none for a public instance | The Workbench's Jira lane |
| `confluence` | The pages of `--space KEY` (optionally narrowed with `--cql`) | `--email` and `--token-env`; none for a public instance | The Workbench's Confluence lane |
| `onedrive` | The files of a drive (`--drive me`), optionally one `--folder` | A bearer token in `--token-env`; there is no anonymous tier | — |
| `grafana` | Dashboards and alert rules, as `grafana/dashboards/<uid>.md` and `grafana/alerts/<uid>.md` | A Viewer service-account token in `--token-env` | Dashboard and alert-rule citations in Incidents |
| `prometheus` | Its rules | None, or a bearer for a proxy that demands one | `atlas metrics`, Alerts & Metrics |
| `jenkins` | Jobs and builds | None where the controller allows it, else `--email <user id>` and `--token-env` | `atlas builds`, Builds |
| `tempo` | The services it saw | None, or a bearer for a proxy | `atlas traces`, Traces |

## Add and Sync a Source

The demo service has one public source: the pull requests and issues of
`inference-gateway/inference-gateway` on GitHub. Adding it validates the
connection and writes the configuration; it pulls nothing:

```sh
atlas source add github --kind github --repo inference-gateway/inference-gateway --token-env GITHUB_TOKEN --window 90d
```

```json
{
  "name": "github",
  "kind": "github",
  "repos": ["inference-gateway/inference-gateway"],
  "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN",
  "credential_rung": "none",
  "credential_reason": "$GITHUB_TOKEN is empty and the gh CLI is not installed",
  "window": "90d",
  "validated": true,
  "validated_by": "connector",
  "next": "atlas source sync github"
}
```

**Credentials are names.** `--token-env` names an environment variable; the
token is read from it at sync time and never stored, so the sources file cannot
leak one. Here the variable is set for the one sync command only.

`atlas source sync` does the work: it pulls everything changed since the stored
cursor, writes each record as a file, and indexes the result as a virtual
repository:

```sh
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) atlas source sync github
```

```json
{
  "name": "github",
  "repo_full_name": "github://github",
  "window": "90d",
  "docs_fetched": 287,
  "docs_written": 287,
  "indexed_files": 287,
  "symbols": 1402,
  "reconciled": true,
  "next_reconcile_at": "2026-11-04T05:45:02Z",
  "duration_ms": 228002
}
```

287 pull requests and issues updated in the last 90 days became 287 files in
`github://github`. A sync that finds nothing new is a no-op, not a new snapshot,
and a sync that fails part-way resumes from its last checkpoint.
`atlas source status` reports what is held:

```sh
atlas source status github
```

```json
{
  "name": "github",
  "kind": "github",
  "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN",
  "token_present": false,
  "credential_rung": "none",
  "repo_full_name": "github://github",
  "docs": 287,
  "window": "90d",
  "oldest_updated": "2026-07-31T09:51:54Z",
  "newest_updated": "2026-10-27T17:54:30Z",
  "last_synced_at": "2026-10-28T05:41:16Z",
  "next_reconcile_at": "2026-11-04T05:45:02Z"
}
```

`token_present` is `false` because the variable was set only for the sync.

## Configure a Monitoring Source from the Dashboard

The monitoring kinds can also be added on **Connectors**. **Configure** opens a
form: a source name, the base URL and the name of the variable that holds the
token. As you type, the card shows the same write two other ways — the CLI
command and the HTTP request.

![Opening Configure on the Grafana card, typing a source name, a base URL and GRAFANA_SA_TOKEN, and the CLI and HTTP spellings filling in](assets/docs/sources/configure-a-source.mp4 "The Grafana form. The token field takes a variable name, and the CLI and POST spellings update as you type. The clip stops before Save.")

**Save & validate** has the service reach the URL and check the configuration
before anything is written; the result appears in the card. A configured card
shows the source's state and offers **Edit** and **Remove**. Log pulls and the
Observe views are covered in [Observe](observe).

## Find Pull Requests and Issues in Answers

Once synced, the records answer like code. Search the virtual repository from
the CLI:

```sh
atlas search --repo github://github --format plain streaming
```

```text
search  mode lexical  total 20
  matches  118  (page limit 20)
  #578: fix(proxy): relay upstream status and body on streaming /proxy requests  section  github/inference-gateway/inference-gateway/pull/578.md:24  :: …
  #695: [BUG] MCP streaming mode leaks tool_call deltas to the client …  section  github/inference-gateway/inference-gateway/issue/695.md:15  :: …
  #696: fix(mcp): keep agent tool-call chunks off the client stream  section  github/inference-gateway/inference-gateway/pull/696.md:24  :: …
  …
```

On **Ask Atlas**, choose **docs** and the `github://github` repository: the
answer quotes the passage verbatim, cites the document by path and line, and
offers **Open in Github ↗** to the original.

![Ask Atlas over github://github for Retry-After header: the best passage is the title of pull request 752, cited as github/inference-gateway/inference-gateway/pull/752.md, with Open document and Open in Github](assets/docs/sources/ask-github-pr.png "Pull request #752 found by Ask Atlas: 6 documents answer, the best passage cited by path and line.")

## See a Source's State in the Dashboard

**System** → **App integrations** → **Integrations** shows each GitHub source
as the service sees it: the repositories it covers, how many records it holds,
its credential, its window, the last sync and the webhook address to paste into
the repository's settings.

![The Integrations card: GitHub with no credential, source github with 287 PRs and issues stored, repo inference-gateway/inference-gateway, credential none, window 90d, last sync, and the webhook URL; Pulse with nothing pushed](assets/docs/sources/github-integration.png "The demo's GitHub source: 287 records, a 90-day window, and no credential in the service's own environment.")

The **Credential** row is the rung the service is on: **env** (the variable the
source names is set in the service's environment), **gh_cli**
(`gh auth token`, used only by a service listening on loopback) or **none**.
The service reads the variable from its own environment — for a background
service, the environment it was started with, not your shell's. The Ask
Workbench's GitHub lane — pull requests, checks and reviews read for a
question — needs that credential. On the demo the service was started without
it, so the lane reads **not connected** under every answer, while the synced
records stay searchable. **Connect** leads to this page.

![The source lanes under a Workbench answer: Atlas 11, Git 3, GitHub not connected, Jira not connected, Confluence not connected, Pulse not connected, each with Connect](assets/docs/sources/workbench-source-lanes.png "The lanes under a Workbench answer on the demo: Atlas and Git answered; GitHub, Jira, Confluence and Pulse are not connected.")

## Keep a Source Current

- **Rolling window.** A Jira or GitHub source pulls only records updated within
  its window — 180 days unless `--window` says otherwise — and the same window
  is the corpus's time-to-live: a record that falls behind it leaves at the next
  sync. Other kinds are unbounded unless you set one; Prometheus refuses one.
  `atlas source set <name> --window 26w` changes it: widening back-fills exactly
  the newly covered range, narrowing prunes locally without a request.
- **Schedule.** A running service resyncs its sources every 15 minutes by
  default (`atlas serve --source-sync-every`); `--sync-every` on a source
  overrides it, and `0` opts that source out. The demo's GitHub source is
  synced by hand:

```sh
atlas source set github --sync-every 0
```

```json
{
  "name": "github",
  "next": "atlas source sync github",
  "sync_every": "0",
  "sync_every_effect": "the serve no longer syncs this source on a schedule; its webhook and `atlas source sync` still do"
}
```

- **Deletions.** A sync removes records the source no longer lists by
  reconciling its membership every 7 days (`--reconcile-every`), or at once with
  `atlas source sync <name> --reconcile`. `--full` re-pulls everything from the
  beginning.
- **Webhooks.** A webhook makes a change visible in seconds instead of at the
  next sync. For Jira, `atlas source webhook <name> --secret-env NAME` prints
  the setup, `--register` creates it through Jira's admin API and `--verify`
  waits for the first delivery. For GitHub, the Integrations card gives the
  address (`/api/v1/sources/<name>/webhook`) for the `pull_request`, `issues`
  and `push` events, signed with `X-Hub-Signature-256`.

## Connect Jira

Jira connects two ways, for two jobs:

- **As a source** — one project materialized into the corpus with the service's
  credential, so tickets are searchable, citable and offered to the Workbench's
  Jira lane. A public instance needs no credential: leave `--email` and
  `--token-env` off.
- **As sign-in** — each person connects their own Atlassian account under
  **System** → **App integrations** → **Jira** and searches Jira live with their
  own permissions. The service must be started with `--jira-oauth` and the
  `ATLAS_JIRA_OAUTH_*` settings.

```sh
atlas source add jira-ops --kind jira --url https://jira.example.com --project OPS \
  --email you@example.com --token-env JIRA_API_TOKEN --window 90d
atlas source sync jira-ops
```

The demo service has neither, and its Jira card says so:

![The Jira card under App integrations: Not connected, Jira sign-in is not configured, Ask your Atlas administrator to enable Jira sign-in for this Command Center](assets/docs/sources/jira-card.png "Jira under App integrations on a service started without --jira-oauth.")

## Remove a Source

```sh
atlas source remove github          # forget how the corpus was fetched; keep the corpus
atlas source remove github --purge  # also delete the materialized files
```

Without `--purge` the files and the indexed snapshots stay, so re-adding the
source resumes where it left off. On **Connectors**, **Remove** does the same
for a monitoring source after a second click to confirm.

## From the API

| Route | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/sources` | Every source with its kind, window, credential rung, document count and sync state |
| `POST /api/v1/sources` | Add or replace a source; the service validates it before writing |
| `DELETE /api/v1/sources/{name}` | Remove a source |
| `POST /api/v1/sources/{name}/webhook` | The webhook door a Jira or GitHub delivery posts to |
| `GET /api/v1/sources/pulse/status` | The findings Pulse has pushed |

Writes need the read-write token where a token is set. See
[Dashboard and API](service) and, for every flag, the [CLI reference](cli).

## Related

- [Ask Workbench](workbench) — where the GitHub, Jira, Confluence and Pulse lanes answer.
- [Search and Ask](search-and-ask) — searching code and documents together.
- [Observe](observe) — log pulls, metrics, builds and traces from the monitoring kinds.
- [Privacy and data](privacy) — what a sync stores and where.

# Observe
URL: https://atlas.aziro.com/docs/observe/

# Observe

Observe connects Atlas to what your running system is doing: the logs it
writes, the alerts that fire, the builds that fail and the traces it records.
Atlas keeps a bounded summary of each — log templates with counts, alert and
query summaries, trace summaries — and ties every line it can back to the file
and function that emits it. Reach for it when something is wrong in production
and you want to go from the symptom to the code in a few clicks.

## Open It

The **OBSERVE** group sits in the dashboard's left rail: **Log Streams**
(`#/logs`), **What Changed** (`#/diff`), **Alerts & Metrics** (`#/alerts`),
**Builds** (`#/builds`), **Incidents** (`#/incidents`) and **Traces**
(`#/traces`). **Live Activity** (`#/events`) is at the top of the rail, under
**COMMAND**.

Each view needs one tool configured. Until it is, the view shows the three ways
to configure that tool instead of data — nothing on these pages is sample data.

| View | Needs | Configure it with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Log Streams**, **What Changed**, **Incidents** | a Grafana Loki or Elasticsearch log pull | `atlas logs pull add` |
| **Alerts & Metrics** | a Prometheus source | `atlas source add <name> --kind prometheus` |
| **Builds** | a Jenkins source | `atlas source add <name> --kind jenkins` |
| **Traces** | a Tempo source | `atlas source add <name> --kind tempo` |

The same settings live in **Fleet › Connectors** (`#/connectors`), and each one
is also a single HTTP `POST`. Whichever way you use, the service checks it can
reach the tool before it saves anything. The pages below were recorded on a
service with one log pull from a local Loki and one Prometheus source:

```sh
atlas logs pull add inference-gateway --source loki --url http://127.0.0.1:3100 \
  --selector '{app="inference-gateway"}' --stream inference-gateway --scope prod --since 7h

atlas source add promlabs --kind prometheus --url https://demo.promlabs.com
atlas source sync promlabs
```

A running `atlas serve` picks a new pull up on its next tick and runs it every
`--every` (default 5m). The source sync turns the Prometheus rules into
documents Atlas can cite; the alerts and queries themselves are asked live. See
[Sources](sources) for the other source kinds.

**About the demo logs.** The log lines in these screenshots were generated for
this guide in the exact JSON shape inference-gateway's logger writes, and
pushed into a local Loki. Every `caller` in them is a real log call in the
repository, so everything Atlas resolves below is real.

## Read What a Stream Is Saying

Open **Log Streams**. Atlas does not store log lines. As each line arrives it
is reduced to a template — the sentence with its ids, times and numbers
replaced by `<*>` — and Atlas keeps, per template, a count per UTC hour, a
severity hint, the caller and a few exemplars with secrets masked. A stream's
whole history stays a few hundred rows however many lines produced it.

![Log Streams showing the inference-gateway stream in scope prod: 655 lines folded into 18 templates, loudest first, with level, hourly sparkline, caller and template](assets/docs/observe/log-streams.png "655 lines of inference-gateway logs from the last 24 hours, folded into 18 templates.")

- The **Streams** rail lists every stream in the selected scope. The dot is the
  state of the pull that feeds it: **fresh**, **stale** (no successful pull
  within two cadences), **pending**, or **no pull**.
- The table is loudest first: **count**, **level**, an **hours** sparkline, the
  **caller** the line names, and the **template**.
- Narrow it with the scope picker, the window (**last 15 min** to **last 7 d**),
  the level, and **contains…** — a literal substring matched on the server, not
  a regex.

In this stream the three error templates that only appear in the last two hours
— `failed to generate tokens`, `<*> status code` and `request timed out` — are
the incident. The 449 `request received` lines are normal traffic.

To see what changed rather than what is loud, open **What Changed**. It
compares two windows of one stream from the stored hourly counts: templates
that are **New in B**, **Gone in B**, and those whose per-minute rate moved.
Pick **Recent window**, **Around an instant** (either side of a deploy) or
**Explicit windows**, then **Compare**.

![What Changed comparing the hour before against the last two hours: three new error templates, none gone, and four templates whose rate changed](assets/docs/observe/what-changed.png "The three groq error templates are new in the last window; route not found doubled.")

Windows widen to whole UTC hours, and the page says so when a window is partial
or starts before the stream was first fed.

## Trace a Log Line to Its Code

Click a template row. The inspector on the right shows the skeleton, a masked
exemplar, the caller and when it was first and last seen, then runs the
**resolve chain**: it maps the exemplar to the file and line that emits it in
the repository you pick (Atlas guesses the repository from the stream name).

![The template inspector for failed to generate tokens, resolved to api/routes.go:805 in ChatCompletionsHandler with a 100% score](assets/docs/observe/log-template-inspector.png "The template resolves to api/routes.go:805, inside ChatCompletionsHandler.")

A hit gives you three next steps: **Symbol Inspector**, **Open in Resolve** and
**Code Map**, then **Impact** for the blast radius of the enclosing function.
**Run RCA** opens the incident that groups this template, if there is one.

![Clicking the request timed out template, the resolve chain landing on api/routes.go:801, then Code Map opening on ChatCompletionsHandler](assets/docs/observe/log-template-to-source.mp4 "From a log template to the handler that logs it, on the Code Map.")

When nothing matches, the chain says so and why (for example, the caller names
a file the selected repository does not carry) instead of guessing a plausible
file.

## Work an Incident

An incident is a group of error and warn templates that share a cause — the
call-site file a structured line names, or the head of the error — across every
stream of a scope, joined with the Prometheus alerts that are firing. The
service recomputes incidents every 2 minutes over the last 24 hours
(`ATLAS_INCIDENTS_EVERY`, `ATLAS_INCIDENTS_WINDOW`); **Refresh** does it now.

![Incidents in scope prod: six open incidents in the rail, the selected one keyed on api/routes.go with four member templates](assets/docs/observe/incidents.png "Six open incidents in scope prod. The selected one groups four templates logged from api/routes.go.")

1. Pick an incident in the rail. They are ordered worst first: severity, then
   lines per hour. An **alert only** row is a firing alert with no matching log
   template.
2. Read the header: rate, state, the grouping key (`caller:api/routes.go`),
   when it was first and last seen, and its **members** — click a member to
   open its template in Log Streams.
3. Scroll to **Evidence**: up to 24 citations, numbered **[n]** — the log
   templates, the code that emits them, config and code lines that name the
   same identifiers, matching docs and alert rules.
4. **Ack** (with an optional note) to say someone is on it, or **Resolve**. A
   resolved incident reopens if one of its members is seen again.

![Selecting the failed to generate tokens incident and scrolling its evidence to the code card for api/routes.go:805 in ChatCompletionsHandler](assets/docs/observe/incident-to-source.mp4 "From an incident to the line of code its evidence cites.")

![The Evidence list with log template cards and the Actions card proposing a ticket, a pull request and an alert rule](assets/docs/observe/incident-evidence.png "Evidence on the left; on the right, the actions Atlas derived from it, each awaiting approval.")

**Generate RCA** asks the configured model for a verdict-first narrative over
the evidence cards; every sentence must cite a card or it is dropped. The
**Actions** card lists what to do next — a ticket draft, a pull request naming
the cited files, an alert rule — as descriptors waiting in the
[Action Queue](skills). Approving one records it for whoever carries it out;
Atlas executes none of them.

## Check Alerts and Query Metrics

Open **Alerts & Metrics**. Each panel is one bounded question to the
Prometheus you configured, asked when the page loads.

![Alerts and Metrics for the promlabs source: three firing or pending alerts, a PromQL summary of request rate by status, and scrape targets by job](assets/docs/observe/alerts-metrics.png "Alerts from the public PromLabs demo, a bounded query, and scrape targets.")

- **Firing** — what fires and pends now, with the rule's summary, labels and
  value.
- **Bounded query** — type a PromQL expression, pick a window and press
  **Run**. The answer is a summary, never a series dump: the step Atlas chose
  so each series stays under its point budget, then **min**, **max**, **avg**
  and **last** per series.
- **Scrape targets** — up and down counts by job and environment, with the last
  error of any target that is down.

## Connect Builds and Traces

**Builds** reads a Jenkins job board — each job's last result, duration and
age — from the controller's Prometheus endpoint (the Prometheus metrics
plugin), anonymously first and with the source's credential only when that is
refused. Per-build console output is a separate Jenkins log pull, folded into
templates like any log. No Jenkins is connected in this demo, so the view shows
how to connect one:

![The Builds view before Jenkins is configured, showing the Connectors path, the CLI command and the HTTP request that configure it](assets/docs/observe/builds-empty.png "Builds with no Jenkins configured.")

**Traces** asks a Tempo four kinds of bounded question: which services have
traces in a window, a TraceQL search (newest first, at most a limit), one trace
summarized on one screen (the services it crossed, the five slowest spans, the
error spans), and a TraceQL metrics query under a point budget. There is no
public Tempo to point this guide at, so here it is before one is connected:

![The Traces view before Tempo is configured, with the command atlas source add tempo --kind tempo --url http://tempo:3200](assets/docs/observe/traces-empty.png "Traces with no Tempo configured.")

```sh
atlas source add tempo --kind tempo --url http://tempo:3200
atlas source add jenkins --kind jenkins --url http://jenkins:8080/jenkins --email ops --token-env ATLAS_JENKINS_TOKEN
```

The view appears as soon as the source is saved; no reload is needed.

## Watch Live Activity

**Live Activity** is every event the service records across its connectors —
index reads, recall turns, snapshot history and hub observations. Each row
shows the time, the connector, what happened, the repository, how it was
served, the tokens it returned and its latency. Filter by connector with the
chips, by tier (**automation**, **exact**, **semantic**, **live**), or with
**Filter events…**.

![Live Activity filtered to the atlas connector: index events for github://github, prometheus://promlabs and inference-gateway](assets/docs/observe/live-activity.png "Filtered to the atlas connector: the index run for inference-gateway and the two source syncs.")

## From the CLI

Every view has a command, and every command answers a bounded question.
Streams the dashboard does not show — lines piped in with `atlas logs ingest` —
are read the same way. A piped line counts in the hour it was ingested; a pull
keeps each line's own time.

```text
$ atlas logs ingest --stream inference-gateway --scope local --source-kind file < gateway-info.log
{ "source": "stdin", "scope": "local", "stream": "inference-gateway", "batches": 1,
  "lines_read": 477, "lines_ingested": 477, "lines_skipped": 0, "templates": 9, … }

$ atlas logs streams
STREAM             SCOPE  KIND  LAST_INGEST           LABELS
inference-gateway  local  file  2026-10-28T06:14:21Z  -
inference-gateway  prod   loki  2026-10-28T05:49:01Z  app=inference-gateway,detected_level=warn,env=prod,service_name=inference-gateway

$ atlas logs templates --stream inference-gateway --scope prod --since 24h --limit 6
COUNT  SEVERITY  LAST_SEEN             CALLER                    SKELETON
449    info      2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  middlewares/logger.go:63  request received
56     error     2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  api/routes.go:805         failed to generate tokens | err <*>:{<*>:<*>,<*>:<*>
56     error     2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  core/provider.go:139      <*> status code | err <*>:{<*>:<*>,<*>:<*>
27     error     2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  api/routes.go:801         request timed out | err context deadline exceeded
18     info      2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  mcp/init.go:403           server reconnection failed | err failed to initialize client post <*> dial tcp <*> connect connection refused
18     info      2026-10-28T05:00:00Z  mcp/init.go:397           attempting server reconnection

$ atlas logs diff --stream inference-gateway --scope prod --window 1h
LIST     COUNT_A  COUNT_B  CHANGE  SEVERITY  CALLER                    SKELETON
new      0        56       new     error     api/routes.go:805         failed to generate tokens | err <*>:{<*>:<*>,<*>:<*>
new      0        56       new     error     core/provider.go:139      <*> status code | err <*>:{<*>:<*>,<*>:<*>
new      0        27       new     error     api/routes.go:801         request timed out | err context deadline exceeded
changed  1        5        +165%   warn      api/routes.go:98          route not found
```

`atlas logsites resolve` is the resolve chain on its own. It accepts raw lines
or skeletons; a line the repository does not emit comes back `matched: false`
with a reason.

```text
$ atlas logsites resolve '{"level":"error","timestamp":"2026-10-28T04:38:38.000Z","caller":"api/routes.go:801","msg":"request timed out","provider":"groq","error":"context deadline exceeded"}' 'failed to reach upstream server'
{
  "commit_sha": "524967508e9d90185c4a1c3540cac0dcda7c580a",
  "results": [
    { "matched": true, "file": "api/routes.go", "line": 801, "symbol": "ChatCompletionsHandler",
      "kind": "method", "score": 1, "reason": "caller",
      "skeleton": "request timed out | err context deadline exceeded" },

      "kind": "method", "score": 1, "reason": "exact_skeleton",
      "skeleton": "failed to reach upstream server" }
  ]
}
```

With no Jenkins or Tempo configured, `atlas builds` and `atlas traces` say
exactly what to add:

```text
$ atlas traces services
atlas: no Tempo source is configured — add one: atlas source add <name> --kind tempo --url http://tempo:3200

$ atlas builds jobs
atlas: builds_source_not_found: no jenkins source is configured — `atlas source add <name> --kind jenkins --url http://jenkins:8080/jenkins --email <jenkins user id> --token-env ATLAS_JENKINS_TOKEN` records one; the board reads only its url
```

Assistants reach the same reads through the MCP tools `logs`, `logsite`,
`metrics`, `builds`, `traces` and `incidents` ([MCP Tools](mcp)). The full flag
list is in the [CLI reference](cli).

## From the API

Each view names its data source on the page. The routes behind them:

- `GET /api/v1/logs/streams`, `/logs/templates`, `/logs/diff`, `/logs/pulls`;
  `POST /api/v1/logs/ingest` and `/logs/pulls`
- `POST /api/v1/resolve` — the resolve chain's first step
- `GET /api/v1/metrics/alerts`, `/metrics/targets`; `POST /api/v1/metrics/query`
- `GET /api/v1/builds` and `GET /api/v1/traces?op=services|search|trace|metrics`
- `GET /api/v1/incidents`, `/incidents/{id}?evidence=true`,
  `/incidents/{id}/actions`; `POST /api/v1/incidents/refresh`;
  `PATCH /api/v1/incidents/{id}` to ack, resolve or reopen

Writes need the read-write token when the service enforces one. See
[Dashboard and HTTP API](service).

## Related

- [Sources](sources) — Prometheus, Jenkins, Tempo, Grafana and the knowledge
  sources Atlas indexes.
- [Impact](impact) — the blast radius of the function a log line resolves to.
- [Skills and automations](skills) — the Action Queue where incident actions
  wait for approval.
- [MCP Tools](mcp) — the Observe tools assistants call.
- [Configuration](configuration) — `ATLAS_INCIDENTS_EVERY`,
  `ATLAS_INCIDENTS_WINDOW` and the log pull token allowlist.
